prs.name: capture-anchored-pacing
prs.title: Anchor thread C's capture pacing to when the display presented (E phase 2, in process on Windows and Mac) and add the capture seams later PRs use
prs.protocol_changes: None on the desktop wire (ALPN stays pb-mapper/desktop/2) and none on the helper pipe: HELPER_PROTOCOL and the .v10 pipe names stay, RemoteBackend reports no present stamp until helper-push adds one. Public SDK, semver-minor: provided Backend methods submitted_picture, capture_poll and video_paused, and the Presented type.
prs.design:
Why. Thread C's pacer (pacer.rs) lays ticks on an even grid unrelated to when the display presents. When the pace equals the present rate (Balanced 60 on a 60 Hz panel, Smooth 120 on 120 Hz, a ProMotion Mac) a picture waits up to a period for the next tick (model: mean 5.8-7.2 ms at 60 Hz and 2.9 ms at 120 Hz, falling to about 1 ms) and the grid drops one present per drift cycle, a visible hitch. airhand anchors its timeline on the present: client/src-tauri/src/host/pace.rs:34-50 (an early window of P/4, creep of at most P/64), stamps from host/capture/dxgi.rs:677-679 converted by host/clock.rs:42-76. This PR does it in process on both hosts (the helper path follows in helper-push) and adds every thread C seam the later PRs need, so none of them re-touches the five #[deny(clippy::missing_trait_methods)] impls.

1. Pacer (pacer.rs). Add `anchored: bool`. `earliest()` = if anchored { max(next - P/4, last + 3P/4) } else { next }. `consume(now, presented: Option<Instant>)`: None keeps today's rule byte for byte and clears `anchored`; a stamp later than now is clamped to now; a stamp older than one period counts as None; Some(at): base = if at >= next - P/4 { max(at, next - P/64) } else { next }; next = base + P; anchored = true. Keep the 3/4-period floor after a stall, ticks skipped only for backpressure, and the long-run bound of pace x 64/63. set_pace is unchanged.

2. Seams. All are provided methods whose defaults keep today's behaviour, each forwarded in Box (backend.rs:228), PlatformBackend and NativeBackend (native.rs:114 and 422), RemoteBackend (oop/client.rs:237) and examples/input_acceptance/guarded.rs:35.
- `pub struct Presented { pub at: Instant, pub presents: u32 }` (Copy, #[non_exhaustive], exported with the other backend types) and `Backend::submitted_picture(&self) -> Option<Presented>`: the present time of the picture the last capture_video submitted and how many presents it covered (1 = none skipped). None for liveness and keyframe repeats and for undated pictures. RemoteBackend returns None.
- `Backend::capture_poll(&self) -> Option<Duration> { self.drain_poll() }`: how often thread C re-polls an armed pull capture. capture_poll_after and the input hot-poll path (worker/capture.rs ~143-176) use it instead of drain_poll, so a source can push encoder output while its capture is still polled (win-mf-output-events relies on this).
- `Backend::video_paused(&mut self, paused: bool) {}`: thread C calls it with true on the transition into the all-paused branch (worker/capture.rs ~236) and with false on the way out, before the resume capture. RemoteBackend implements an explicit no-op (DXGI is pull and runs nothing while paused; no helper message). mac-capture-cadence implements it.
- VideoSource (platform/mod.rs): `fn presented(&self) -> Option<Presented> { None }`; `fn drain_poll(&self) -> Option<Duration> { Self::DRAIN }`; `const CAPTURE_POLL: Option<Duration> = Self::DRAIN;` with `fn capture_poll(&self) -> Option<Duration> { Self::CAPTURE_POLL }` (instance methods so one encoder instance can fall back to polling); `fn paused(&mut self, paused: bool) {}`; `fn retune(&mut self, display: &Display, limits: VideoLimits) -> Result<bool> { Ok(false) }`. PlatformBackend forwards each to the open source and uses the consts when none is open.
- configure_video (native.rs:151-156): validate the limits; if a source is open and `retune(&context.display, limits)` returns Ok(true), keep it, otherwise drop it as today; store the limits either way. A context change still rebuilds through capture_video's context compare (native.rs:191-206). Thread C still sets keyframe on a limits change.
- platform/synthetic.rs: SynVideo implements retune (true for an fps-only change, false for a size change) and gains a dated push mode (pictures stamped at a configurable rate and drift, waking its Waker) for the tests.

3. Thread C (worker/capture.rs, worker.rs; static dispatch only, Engine<B: Backend>). capture_at() uses pacer.earliest(). The submit path calls consume(now, backend.submitted_picture().map(|p| p.at)); the backpressure and skip paths pass None. The helper drain long-poll bound (HELPER_DRAIN_WAIT_MAX at worker/capture.rs:366) uses capture_at() instead of pacer.next().

4. macOS (platform/macos/capture.rs, video.rs). In the ScreenCaptureKit output callback, under the existing Latest lock (capture.rs:138-144), store `arrived = Instant::now()` and count Complete pictures, Idle samples and pictures replaced before a take in capture::Shared (no allocation). take() returns, for a fresh picture, its arrival and the number of Complete pictures since the last take; MacVideo::presented returns them for a fresh submit and None for repeats. SCStreamFrameInfoDisplayTime feeds diagnostics only, converted by its age against mach_absolute_time with the cached timebase (airhand host/clock.rs:29-40); no CMSync feature.

5. Windows in process (platform/windows/video/mod.rs and mod.rs; add Win32_System_Performance to the windows crate features). Convert LastPresentTime by its age: QueryPerformanceCounter now minus the stamp, with QueryPerformanceFrequency cached in a OnceLock; a negative age (read-order race) counts as 0, an age over 1 s gives None; result Instant::now() - age (std's Instant is QPC-based on Windows, so this is exact up to read skew). Keep `latest_at` and the summed AccumulatedFrames beside latest_pending; a picture left pending by Full or an empty allocator keeps its old stamp and consume ignores it once it is older than a period. Fresh pictures use the present Instant, kept strictly increasing, for pts_us and the sample duration; repeats use now. Statistics and video_bench gain `coalesced_presents` (sum of AccumulatedFrames - 1 over fresh acquires). First frame (R3-first-frame; airhand host/capture/dxgi.rs:632-633): in acquire (video/mod.rs ~571-618), when `latest` is None and the resource is present, copy it as a new image whatever LastPresentTime says, leave it undated, and log once per encoder at debug the first acquire's LastPresentTime and AccumulatedFrames. video_bench mirrors the new pacer and prints present-to-submit p50/p95.

6. Diagnostics. A once-a-second debug event `desktop_capture_pacing` from worker/window.rs roll(): present-to-submit wait p50/p95 (submit Instant - Presented.at), dated share of submits, captures/s, presents/s, coalesced presents/s (sum of presents - 1), empty polls/s. Fixed buffers, no allocation per frame.

7. Docs. Reword rule 2 of 'Video pipeline and performance model' (docs/remote-desktop.md ~1218-1222) and the host capture paragraphs, keeping its sub-rules (skips only for backpressure, the long-run rate, the 3/4-period floor, creep of at most P/64); the constants table; the new Backend methods. No model figures in docs; the CHANGELOG bullet says what changes and gains figures only from the device runs.

prs.name: mac-wake-display
prs.title: Mac host: wake a sleeping, unlocked display when a viewer's capture starts, resumes or finds no picture
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. The Mac host keeps the display awake only while it captures (platform/macos/timer.rs:28-40, NSActivity IdleDisplaySleepDisabled); it never wakes a display that is already asleep, and nothing calls IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity or checks CGDisplayIsAsleep. ScreenCaptureKit delivers no picture from a sleeping display, and input is admitted only for a presented frame produced within 2 s (auth.rs:11, 74-80), so the viewer cannot even wake the Mac by moving the mouse: the session shows nothing and rebuilds capture in a loop until someone touches the Mac. airhand wakes the display (client/src-tauri/src/host/power.rs:232-250, like `caffeinate -u`) and skips a closed lid (power.rs:255-260).

1. New platform/macos/power.rs.
- extern IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity and IOPMAssertionRelease with #[link(name = "IOKit", kind = "framework")], following desktop.rs:23-28 (objc2-io-kit's pwr_mgt would be a new direct crate).
- A pure `WakeLimiter` with an injected Instant: at most one declaration every 2 s. Build and test it on every platform, like geometry.rs (mod.rs:18-30).
- `wake(ids) -> bool`: for each id where CGDisplayIsAsleep (CGDisplayConfiguration feature, already on), declare kIOPMUserActiveLocal activity, reusing the returned assertion id as the header asks (a static Mutex<(Option<Instant>, IOPMAssertionID)>). Returns whether any display was asleep.
- Skip a built-in display (CGDisplayIsBuiltin) while the lid is closed: read AppleClamshellState from IOPMrootDomain as airhand power.rs:255-260 does; otherwise the panel lights behind the lid for about 10 s and goes dark again in a cycle.
2. Call sites, each only after desktop::available() has passed (unlocked, on the console); a locked Mac stays dark by design.
- (a) Macos::open (mod.rs ~153), before MacDesktop::open: if any online display (CGGetOnlineDisplayList) is asleep, wake it, then poll every 100 ms for up to 3 s for the selected display to become active (airhand waits up to 3 s before Hello).
- (b) MacVideo::open (video.rs:50-74), before Stream::start: wake(display.id). This also covers a resume, whose capture reopens here.
- (c) On MacVideo's no-picture failure (video.rs:96-103), or a DisplayLost from capture::display, while CGDisplayIsAsleep(id): wake it and fail with CaptureFailed 'the display is asleep; waking it'; the 200 ms retry then reopens.
3. Release the reused assertion id when the last timer guard is released (timer.rs:43-53).
4. Docs: 'Sharing a Mac' and the macOS host paragraph in docs/remote-desktop.md; the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) where it describes a sleeping Mac; a CHANGELOG bullet.
(Merged duplicate R4-mac-host-wake-display: its resume case is (b), its no-frame case is (c) with the 2 s limiter.)

prs.name: mac-session-check-cache
prs.title: Mac host: reuse a passing session and geometry check for 16 ms across capture and cursor verifies
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. Every Mac capture and cursor verify reads the session dictionary and display geometry from WindowServer (about 48 us). View-only at 60 fps that is about 120 capture plus 125 cursor verifies a second, 13-14 ms of thread C CPU a second plus WindowServer's side.

1. platform/mod.rs Desktop gains provided methods defaulting to today's behaviour: `fn prepare_recent(&mut self, on_switch: impl FnOnce()) -> Result<()> { self.prepare(on_switch) }` and `fn display_matches_recent(&mut self, expected: &Display) -> Result<bool> { self.display_matches(expected) }`.
2. native.rs: `verify(expected, recent: bool)`. capture_video (~188, ~218) and cursor (~257, ~261) pass recent = true; input_in_context (~278) passes false. display() and context() stay fresh, so the 100 ms context check and every input read WindowServer: the injection boundary is unchanged.
3. MacDesktop (platform/macos/desktop.rs) overrides both with a small pure `Reuse` policy struct (injected Instant), placed so it builds and tests on every platform like geometry.rs: a passing session check and the Geometry it read are reused while now < checked + 16 ms; a failure is never cached and clears the reuse; every fresh prepare, display or display_matches call refreshes it.
4. Unit tests of the policy on every platform: call counts, failures never cached, input always fresh.
5. Docs: 'inside each capture' becomes 'within 16 ms of each capture'; the injection-boundary wording stays.

prs.name: mac-vt-submit-thread
prs.title: Mac host: call VideoToolbox from its own submit thread and keep at most two units in flight
prs.protocol_changes: None (internal to platform/macos; no helper pipe on macOS, no wire or FFI change).
prs.design:
Why. VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame is synchronous whenever the encoded size is 16-aligned. Measured here (synthetic surfaces, pb-mapper settings, low latency): 1920x1200 5.3-5.5 ms, 2560x1440 7.0-7.8 ms, 2560x1664 7.7-8.6 ms, 3008x1952 10.9 ms, 3328x2160 13.0 ms, 3840x2160 14.4-15.2 ms; unaligned sizes return in 0.02-0.05 ms. Thread C sits in that call, so input queued meanwhile waits: estimated input_wait p99 about 7.3 ms at 1440p and 14 ms at 4K, against the documented p99 <= 5 ms gate (docs/remote-desktop.md:1705-1708), and the VideoSource::submit contract ('without blocking') is broken. At unaligned sizes VideoToolbox is asynchronous and ENCODER_DEPTH 4 lets four units queue: at pace 120, 3024x1964 dwell is 43-62 ms with four and 20-23 ms with two at the same frame rate (scratchpad notes r2rev_queue_big.txt, r2rev_3340.txt). airhand encodes on its own per-stream thread (client/src-tauri/src/host/pipeline.rs:96-98, host/encoder/vt.rs:416-445) apart from input (host/input/thread.rs:82-96).

In platform/macos/encoder.rs and video.rs:
1. Submit thread. Spawn one std::thread 'pb-mapper-vt-submit' per Encoder in Encoder::build after prepare_to_encode_frames (encoder.rs:352-357), not for the encodes() probe (199-215). Every VideoToolbox session call happens on it: EncodeFrame, the AverageBitRate and DataRateLimits sets and ForceKeyFrame (later PRs route their property sets here too). No lock is held across a VT call. It owns a CFRetained<VTCompressionSession> clone, the prebuilt ForceKeyFrame dictionary and an Arc<Shared>, carried by a SendSession newtype with a SAFETY note (CF objects are retained and released atomically; every VT call is serialised on this thread), like `unsafe impl Send for Picture` (capture.rs:72-73). Each job runs inside objc2::rc::autoreleasepool. The thread keeps thread C's QoS class: no separate priority experiment (F, thread priority, was withdrawn after measurement).
2. One-slot mailbox in Shared, under the existing state mutex plus a parking_lot Condvar: `job: Option<Job { picture: CFRetained<CVPixelBuffer>, pts_us, keyframe, duplicate, token }>` (a CFRetain: no pixel copy, no per-frame allocation, no VecDeque), `rate: Option<u32>` (latest wins), `in_call: bool`, `c_waiting: bool`.
3. Encoder::encode (450-497) computes pts and pushes Pending with at = now exactly as today, so dwell, late() and the OUTPUT_WAIT stall check (506-515) are unchanged; then places the Job, notifies and returns Ok(()). The thread runs encode_frame and its error cleanup (472-494); a non-zero status pops the matching Pending, sets state.failure and wakes thread C, and drain() surfaces it through codec_error, so H.265's EncoderFailed path is unchanged. After each call it clears in_call and, when c_waiting is set, clears it and wakes thread C.
4. Encoder::set_bitrate (410-431) stores `rate = Some(bitrate)`, caches self.bitrate and notifies; the thread applies AverageBitRate and DataRateLimits before its next EncodeFrame, or at once when idle; an AverageBitRate refusal becomes state.failure. This takes the 0.17-2.6 ms property sets off thread C.
5. Two gates in MacVideo::submit (video.rs:85-109), replacing `pending() >= ENCODER_DEPTH`:
- `Encoder::in_flight()` = state.pending.len() plus a mailbox job (finished-but-undrained `ready` units and the failure flag excluded). Add `const VT_IN_FLIGHT: usize = 2` in video.rs with a doc comment citing the measurement and `const _: () = assert!(VT_IN_FLIGHT + 1 < ENCODER_DEPTH)`. When in_flight() >= VT_IN_FLIGHT, return Ok(true): backpressure spends the tick, as measured for depth 2.
- Otherwise, when `Encoder::busy()` (a job waits in the mailbox or the thread is inside a call; it sets c_waiting), return Ok(false) without taking the picture and keep self.keyframe. The tick stays armed (worker/capture.rs:335-347), so the newest picture is taken the moment the thread is free. Returning Ok(true) here would cut 4K at pace 120 from about 66 fps to the grid's 60.
- Leave the worker's generic gate (worker/capture.rs:302), capture.rs's QUEUE_DEPTH assertion and Windows' MAX_IN_FLIGHT unchanged.
6. MacVideo::idle_until (110-120): while busy return Some(Instant::now() + LATE_OUTPUT); None would mean due now and spin a push source (DRAIN None). The real wake comes from the thread.
7. pending() = in-session + ready + a filled mailbox + failure.
8. Drop (520-526): put Stop in the mailbox, notify and join bounded by LATE_OUTPUT (a synchronous encode is at most about 25 ms). The thread invalidates the session after its last call. If the join times out the thread is detached; it owns its clones, so the refcon (Arc::as_ptr of Shared) stays valid until it exits.
9. Diagnostics (host log only): once a second the thread traces `macos_encoder_load` {call_p50_us, call_p99_us, units, gate_ticks (spent on the in-flight gate), armed_refusals (busy), peak_in_flight}; mac-vt-rate-control's H.265 switch rule reads these counters. Also land here the Phase 0 trace mac-vt-padded-capture needs: at MacVideo's first picture, CVPixelBufferGetExtendedPixels, CVPixelBufferGetHeightOfPlane and CVPixelBufferGetBytesPerRowOfPlane for both planes, and IOSurfaceGetAllocSize.
10. Docs: the Mac paragraph of 'Host: capture and encoding' (the encoder runs on its own submit thread; its VT gate is two in flight, and why; today's text says four cover nearly four periods), the input_wait paragraph; a CHANGELOG bullet. The worker.rs:1-5 claim and the VideoSource::submit contract become true again without edits.

prs.name: mac-vt-rate-control
prs.title: Mac host: QP up to 51, re-send a dropped final picture, H.265 standard rate control above the low-latency knee, and the Timestamp rate model on Apple silicon
prs.protocol_changes: None (Stats.rate_model already carries timestamp).
prs.design:
Why. (a) VideoToolbox's low-latency rate control silently drops up to 33-50% of submitted frames on full-motion content at Balanced or Smooth budgets (scratchpad notes r2rev_maxqp*.txt), taking frame-rate control away from QoS. (b) When the dropped picture is the last change (a typed character, the end of a scroll), common in the 0.5-1.8 s after an IDR at 4 Mbit/s or less, the viewer keeps the previous one until the 250 ms liveness repeat. (c) Low latency cannot sustain large sizes at 120: 4K@120 gives 67-71 fps, 3024x1964@120 92-95, where standard rate control reached 110-120 fps (harness, scratchpad vt120*.swift). (d) Mac sessions start at the Nominal rate model while VideoToolbox budgets per second of wall-clock pts, so a reduced pace overspends 1.3-2.75x until the latch fires, and a frame-rate cut sheds no bandwidth.

Commits in this order, measurement first.
0. Ignored release tests on the unchanged code (platform/macos/tests.rs or a new cfg(test) module beside it): video_toolbox_drops, video_toolbox_resubmit, video_toolbox_120, video_toolbox_rate_step, and a follow-pace mode of video_toolbox_rate_model_{h264,h265} (see measurement).
1. MaxAllowedFrameQP 51 (R2-vt-max-qp-51). Look up kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MaxAllowedFrameQP with cf::symbol like LOW_LATENCY (encoder.rs:104-107). prs.name: mac-capture-cadence
prs.title: Mac host: ScreenCaptureKit cadence from the display's refresh and the live pace, a 2 fps pause, a faster start, a filled frame, and no capture rebuild on an fps-only limits change
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. Stream::start sets minimumFrameInterval = 0.9/max_fps (capture.rs:363-367). Under strict gating ScreenCaptureKit rounds each delivered interval up to whole refresh periods, so a 144 Hz Mac delivers 72 to a 120 fps viewer and 48 to a 60 fps one; 75/100/165 Hz give 37.5/50/55 at 60 (this Mac's display is 144 Hz). Meanwhile at a pace below the refresh SCK still composes every frame thread C will drop; a paused room keeps SCK at 60-120 frames a second; every start or retry enumerates every window of every app; a sub-pixel aspect mismatch leaves a darkened edge row; and any change of the room's limits (a 60 Hz phone pausing in a room with a 120 Hz Mac viewer) stops and restarts SCK and VideoToolbox, freezing the other viewers' picture.

Step 0 (decides the rate claims): an ignored test `sck_cadence` in platform/macos/tests.rs, run on a 144 Hz display with a full-screen animation at the display's rate, 5 s at each interval: 15 ms (today), 10.4 ms (floor rule), 3.5 ms and 0; print Complete callbacks a second and a histogram of SCStreamFrameInfoDisplayTime deltas in vsyncs. Strict gating shows about 48, 72, 144, 144 a second; if 15 ms already gives 60 or more, drop the frame-rate claim (the GPU saving of following the pace still stands).

1. Cadence (R1-sck-refresh-interval with R1-sck-interval-follows-pace; R1's corrected rule, chosen over the duplicate R10-mac-sck-frame-interval). New pure platform/macos/cadence.rs, built and tested everywhere like geometry.rs (mod.rs:18-30): `pub(crate) fn frame_interval(refresh_hz: Option<f64>, target_fps: u32, max_fps: u32) -> Duration`. With a refresh: m = refresh/target; if m is within 1% of an integer k >= 1, n = k (SCK delivers at the pace and the anchored pacer takes each picture on arrival); otherwise n = max(1, floor(m/4)) (every vsync for any m below 8, the least staleness). Interval = (n - 0.5)/refresh. Without a refresh: today's 9/(10 x max_fps), and the pace is not followed. If Step 0 shows the GPU saving matters more than about 3 ms of latency, the fallback n = max(1, floor(m)) for m >= 2 is chosen from measured WindowServer and GPU numbers only.
2. Refresh source (capture.rs; OS calls only here): CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate(CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode(id)) when above 1; else CVDisplayLinkCreateWithCGDisplay and CVDisplayLinkGetNominalOutputVideoRefreshPeriod (add objc2-core-video's 'CVDisplayLink' feature in the workspace Cargo.toml; #[allow(deprecated)] with the reason: the only off-main-thread source for built-in panels); else None. NSScreen is main-thread only, so not used.
3. Stream::start takes frame_interval(refresh, rate.pace_fps.min(max_fps), max_fps). An info event `macos_capture_opened` {refresh_hz, link_period_us, n, interval_us, drift_ppm} where drift_ppm compares n x the display-link period with the grid period (positive: this display got the sawtooth on the old grid).
4. Live retune: Stream keeps (width, height) and the retained background colour (Running._background). `Stream::set_interval(Duration)` builds a fresh configuration with configuration(width, height, true), the same QUEUE_DEPTH and that background, and calls updateConfiguration_completionHandler (SCStream.rs:971) inside an autoreleasepool without waiting; the completion block retains the configuration and logs a failure; at most one update is in flight, a newer target is stored and applied from the completion. MacVideo keeps refresh (re-read at most once a second) and the current n; set_rate (video.rs:78-81) computes n from rate.pace_fps.min(max_fps); a faster cadence applies at once, a slower one only after holding 1 s (pure hysteresis helper with a test); open passes the current pace. Correctness gate before shipping: a change SCK throttles must arrive at the next allowed vsync, not be lost (a 120 Hz Mac with a 60 Hz viewer relies on this today).
5. Pause throttle (R1-sck-pause-throttle): MacVideo implements VideoSource::paused (thread C already calls Backend::video_paused on the all-paused transitions, from capture-anchored-pacing): set_interval(500 ms) while paused, the pace cadence on resume, applied before the resume IDR is taken; the resume IDR still comes from Latest at once.
6. Fast start (R1-sck-fast-start): capture.rs display(id) calls getShareableContentExcludingDesktopWindows_onScreenWindowsOnly_completionHandler(true, true, ..) (SCShareableContent.rs:281): only displays are read and the filter is display-based with no exclusions, so the picture is unchanged. No cross-stream cache; the still path keeps its own (still.rs:21-38). A debug event times display(id) and start-to-first-Complete.
7. Fill the frame (R1-sck-fill-aspect): in configuration() (capture.rs:285-318) call setPreservesAspectRatio(false) where SCStreamConfiguration responds to the selector (macOS 14+), following 307-309; keep the opaque black background for older systems; extend capture_without_a_pointer_stays_opaque (tests.rs:227-258) to assert the flag where the selector exists. Stills share the configuration.
8. Keep capture across an fps-only limits change (R1-mac-keep-capture-across-limits): MacVideo implements VideoSource::retune (PlatformBackend::configure_video already calls it, from capture-anchored-pacing): return false unless scaled_size(display, new limits) equals its encode size; otherwise store max_fps (the cadence fallback), set kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ExpectedFrameRate live on the encoder's submit thread (best effort, a hint), re-apply the SCK cadence for the current pace and return true. Thread C still sets keyframe on a limits change (the joining viewer needs that IDR). Windows keeps the default rebuild.
9. Tests: the cadence table (144/60 n=1, 120/60 n=2, 119.88/60 n=2, 59.94/60 n=1, 240/60 n=4, 60/25 n=1, 60/30 n=2, None -> 0.9/max); a strict-gating simulator over vsync-aligned frames for refresh in {48, 59.94, 60, 75, 90, 100, 119.88, 120, 144, 165, 240} and targets 20..120 asserting delivered >= min(target, refresh) x 0.99 and exactly the target at exact multiples; the hysteresis; a worker test that a paused second slot with lower fps keeps the source (SynVideo).
10. Docs: the macOS paragraph of 'Host: capture and encoding', the constants table, 'Remote resolution' / shared-stream text; CHANGELOG bullets only with device-measured figures.

prs.name: win-encoder-settings
prs.title: Windows host: H.264 High with CABAC (Baseline fallback and latch, SPS reorder fix), QualityVsSpeed and display-remoting scenario by measurement, and GPU priority under load
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire or the helper pipe. The H.264 bitstream profile changes from Baseline to (Constrained) High, which Mac hosts already send to every viewer; the decision stays inside the process that owns the encoder.
prs.design:
Why. Windows hosts encode H.264 as Baseline with CAVLC; CABAC codes the same quality in about a tenth fewer bits (airhand's own figure, consistent with the literature) and High adds the 8x8 transform. Every Windows-hosted session that ends on H.264 (Windows viewers without the HEVC extension, Linux viewers without hardware HEVC, any session after an H.265 failure) is sharper at the same bits per frame. QualityVsSpeed is fixed at 0 and the display-remoting scenario is never set, though either may buy quality per bit at little dwell on some vendors. Under a GPU-saturating 3D load, capture copies and the video processor queue behind the foreground app.

A. H.264 High + CABAC (codec.rs Codec::activate). When kind == H264 and a new process latch H264_HIGH_FAILED (AtomicBool beside H265_FAILED) is clear: request eAVEncH264VProfile_High (try eAVEncH264VProfile_UCConstrainedHigh first where an MFT accepts it); set CODECAPI_AVEncH264CABACEnable = true before the media types, best effort. Apply the H.265 B-frame rule: an encoder implementing CODECAPI_AVEncMPVDefaultBPictureCount must take 0 and read 0 back, or this build uses Baseline; an E_NOTIMPL encoder relies on the required CODECAPI_AVLowLatencyMode and the per-output reorder check. If SetOutputType refuses High, reset CABAC, set Base and retry once. In collect (video/mod.rs:445-449) a reorder from an H.264 High encoder sets H264_HIGH_FAILED before returning the error, so the retry rebuilds at Baseline. A pure `pick_h264_profile` with a table test.
B. SPS reorder (replaces the researcher's step 2). New neutral crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/codec/sps.rs: RBSP unescape and re-escape, exp-Golomb reader and writer, and an H.264 SPS parser through the VUI (including high-profile chroma_format_idc, bit depths and scaling lists) with a writer that copies the remaining bits. In ParameterSets::observe (codec/annexb.rs), only when bitstream_restriction is absent or max_num_reorder_frames != 0, rewrite the VUI to max_num_reorder_frames = 0 and max_dec_frame_buffering = num_ref_frames, once per SPS change (never per packet); leave the constraint flags alone. Unit-test it on committed VideoToolbox-made and NVENC-made SPS samples. mac-vt-padded-capture extends this module with HEVC and cropping.
C. Read-back event `desktop_video_encoder_opened` {rate_control, quality_vs_speed, scenario, b_frames, cabac, profile, sps_reorder} from Encoder::build, copied into Statistics.
D. QualityVsSpeed and scenario (R9-win-quality-vs-speed): take QualityVsSpeed from EncoderSettings and set it where it is set today, before the media types, and read it back; video_bench `--qvs` reaching new_with_size and new_exact; `--scenario display-remoting` sets CODECAPI_AVScenarioInfo = eAVScenarioInfo_DisplayRemoting before the media types (Microsoft defines it for screen-remoting encoders; neither pb-mapper nor airhand sets it). Per adapter VendorId and size, adopt a default only where the device sweep shows PSNR at equal bitrate up >= 0.3 dB (or bytes at equal QP down >= 5%) with median encode up <= 1 ms at 4K60 and dwell p95 <= a quarter of the frame period at the session's largest size and pace (4.2 ms at 4K60), and the rate model staying nominal; otherwise keep 0 and no scenario.
E. GPU priority (R3-gpu-priority), new platform/windows/gpu_priority.rs: a counted guard held while the encoder streams, like TimerResolution. In build(), device.cast::<IDXGIDevice>()?.SetGPUThreadPriority(7), ignoring failure; the first holder reads the current class and calls D3DKMTSetProcessSchedulingPriorityClass(GetCurrentProcess(), HIGH) through the windows Wdk Direct3D bindings or GetProcAddress on gdi32; the last release restores the old class; never REALTIME (it can starve DWM); log the outcome once. EncoderSettings.gpu_priority defaults off, video_bench `--gpu-priority`; switch the default on only if the device run under a GPU-saturating load, with HAGS on and off, in process and through the helper, lowers encoder dwell p95 or present-to-output time without lowering the foreground load's frame rate by more than 5%.
F. video_bench: --h264-profile base|high, --qvs, --scenario, --gpu-priority, --dump-source, a GDI-text still pattern.
G. Docs: Windows encoder paragraph, Diagnostics (desktop_video_encoder_opened), 'Encoder rate model per GPU' sweep results; docs/benchmarks record; CHANGELOG bullet (sharper Windows-hosted H.264) with measured numbers.

prs.name: mac-vt-padded-capture
prs.title: Mac host: capture unaligned sizes into a 16-padded surface and crop them in the SPS, so VideoToolbox takes its fast path at every size
prs.protocol_changes: None: H.264 and HEVC carry the visible size in the SPS (frame_cropping / conformance_window), which every viewer's decoder already honours (every 1920x1080 stream today is coded 1088 and cropped). VideoFormat.width/height keep meaning the content size.
prs.design:
Why. VideoToolbox encodes a 16-unaligned picture through an internal copy. Measured here with synthetic surfaces, padded against unpadded at the native size, 60 fps dwell p50: 3024x1964 12.15/11.90 -> 10.93/10.80 ms; 1920x1080 5.04/5.98 -> 4.30/4.35 ms; at pace 120, 3024x1964 unaligned runs at 19 ms dwell with two in flight against about 11 ms aligned at the same ~90 fps (scratchpad notes r2rev_ext.txt, r2rev_align.txt). These are the commonest Mac hosts at the default Native limit: MacBook Pro 14 (3024x1964), MacBook Air 13 (2940x1912), 1920x1080 externals, and scaled sizes keep their exact aspect. kVTCompressionPropertyKey_CleanAperture does not write the crop (re-parsed SPS stays 1088/1968; scratchpad r2rev_clap.txt), so the host rewrites it.

Phase 0 (gate): read the device trace mac-vt-submit-thread added (CVPixelBufferGetExtendedPixels, plane heights and bytes per row, IOSurfaceGetAllocSize at the first picture). If ScreenCaptureKit's surfaces already declare 16-padding, stop and record the result: this item then has no effect.

Phase 1:
1. Sizes, in MacVideo::open: content = scaled_size(...) exactly; coded = each dimension rounded up to a multiple of 16.
2. ScreenCaptureKit (capture.rs configuration): width and height = coded; destinationRect = (0, 0, content) (macOS 12.3+), so the display is written 1:1, or scaled as today, into the top-left; with preservesAspectRatio false (from mac-capture-cadence) it fills that rect exactly; the remainder takes the configured opaque black background.
3. Encoder: the VideoToolbox session is created at the coded size; VideoFormat.width/height report the content size.
4. codec/sps.rs (created by win-encoder-settings for H.264): add the HEVC SPS parser (profile_tier_level with sub-layers, chroma_format_idc, picture size) and writers: H.264 frame_cropping_flag = 1 with right and bottom offsets in CropUnit 2 for 4:2:0 frame-only streams, HEVC conformance_window_flag with conf_win_right/bottom_offset in units of 2, copying every remaining bit (VUI included).
5. Output path (encoder.rs): rewrite the parameter sets once per CMFormatDescription, cached by its pointer, so only keyframes carry them and nothing runs per packet; they go to annex_b (encoder.rs:706-717).
6. Fallback: a parse failure at the first keyframe sets padding off for the process and fails the session once; the rebuild uses today's exact size.
7. Input and cursor mapping use display geometry and a proportional picture, so they stay exact.
8. Docs: the Mac paragraph and 'H.265 and H.264'; CHANGELOG bullet with measured dwell.
(This supersedes R2-vt-align-scaled-size, dropped: rounding the content size down distorts the aspect by up to 0.8% and covers scaled sizes only.)

prs.name: win-keep-awake
prs.title: Windows host: keep the display and the system awake while a viewer session captures, and wake a dark display when it starts
prs.protocol_changes: None: the helper worker runs the same video source, so no helper request is needed and HELPER_PROTOCOL is unchanged.
prs.design:
Why. A view-only viewer's picture freezes when the host's display-off timeout fires (often 5-15 minutes; DXGI gets no new pictures), a Modern Standby laptop sleeps mid-session and kills it, and a controller who only moves the pointer neither resets the idle timer nor wakes the display (SetCursorPos is not input). The Mac host already holds an NSActivity with IdleDisplaySleepDisabled (platform/macos/timer.rs:28-40).

Design (kept inside platform/windows, so it needs neither oop/server.rs nor timer.rs):
1. New platform/windows/power.rs: a process-wide keeper driven by `touch()`, an atomic store of the time (no allocation, safe on the data path). The Windows VideoSource's submit (platform/windows/mod.rs, VideoSource::submit) calls power::touch() on every call, in process and in the helper worker alike, so it runs exactly while a session captures.
2. The first touch starts one watchdog thread that parks on a condvar while idle (no wake-ups when nothing shares). On the first touch after at least 2 s without one, it calls PowerCreateRequest (simple reason string) and PowerSetRequest for PowerRequestDisplayRequired and PowerRequestSystemRequired, and SetThreadExecutionState(ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED) once to turn a dark display on, so a session that starts or resumes with the display off gets its first picture without local input. While touches keep coming (checked each 1 s) it holds. 2 s after the last touch (pause, close, pipe loss, worker exit) it calls PowerClearRequest for both, CloseHandle, and parks. Drop and process exit release.
3. Log acquire and release once each at debug.
4. Add the needed windows crate features (Win32_System_Power, Win32_System_Threading).
5. Docs: Windows hosting paragraph, the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) where display sleep is mentioned; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: win-mf-output-events
prs.title: Windows host: wake thread C on the encoder's events instead of polling them every 2 ms, and keep a tick armed while the encoder has not asked for input
prs.protocol_changes: None. The helper's v10 `submitted: false` already means 'keep the tick armed'.
prs.design:
Why. Thread C polls the MFT's events every 2 ms while a unit is pending, so each unit reaches it 0.3-1 ms late on average (about 0.35 ms for NVIDIA 1080p, 0.9 ms for 3.1 ms 4K encodes, about 1 ms on slow iGPUs), and it wakes every 2 ms meanwhile. Separately, Encoder::submit returns Full whenever need_input == 0 (video/mod.rs:506-508) and Full spends the tick (mod.rs:108-116); some MFTs send METransformNeedInput only once ProcessOutput released the previous output (mod.rs:481-484), so an encode taking between one and two periods halves the frame rate.

1. codec.rs: after BEGIN_STREAMING, if the MFT exposes IMFShutdown (async MFTs must), start a watcher thread: CoInitializeEx(MTA), loop on IMFMediaEventGenerator::GetEvent(0) (blocking). It is the only event consumer (another GetEvent caller gets MF_E_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS). need_input and have_output become AtomicU32s shared with thread C: the watcher increments them, enforces the bounds (need_input over 64, have_output over MAX_IN_FLIGHT) and failed statuses as a sticky failure thread C's next drain returns, and calls Waker::wake after HaveOutput and NeedInput; ProcessInput and ProcessOutput decrement. events() reads the atomics. Codec's Drop: IMFShutdown::Shutdown, join the watcher (its pending GetEvent returns), then release. An MFT without IMFShutdown gets no watcher and keeps today's 2 ms polling.
2. video/mod.rs: build() takes the Waker passed to VideoSource::open.
3. platform/windows/mod.rs (seams from capture-anchored-pacing): VideoSource::drain_poll(&self) returns None when the watcher runs and Some(DRAIN_POLL) otherwise; CAPTURE_POLL stays Some(DRAIN_POLL), so the armed DXGI polls (worker/capture.rs:143-176) keep their 2 ms until win-present-waiter. Push sources are drained at every CONTEXT_CHECK_INTERVAL context check, as the Mac's are, so the OUTPUT_WAIT stall check holds; add no extra safety poll.
4. The helper's drain long-poll keeps its 1 ms sleep loop (oop/server.rs:291); helper-push removes it, so do not add an interim condvar there.
5. Submit::Waiting (R3-need-input-armed): spends_tick() false, returned for need_input == 0 && pending.len() < MAX_IN_FLIGHT, before any acquire. Full remains for MAX_IN_FLIGHT and an empty sample allocator. Thread C retries at its 2 ms armed poll, or at once when the watcher's NeedInput wakes it. An MFT that never asks is still failed by FIRST_SUBMIT_WAIT (mod.rs:630-636). Statistics gains a Waiting counter.
6. video_bench: a HaveOutput-to-ProcessOutput delay histogram, the median 'drain that returned a unit', Waiting/s, thread C wakes/s.
7. Docs: the Windows host paragraph (encoder output is pushed), Diagnostics; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: win-capture-convert
prs.title: Windows host: convert straight from the duplication surface, keep an NV12 copy for repeats, share rotated displays, crop an odd edge, and ask for quality when downscaling
prs.protocol_changes: None. A rotated display's video simply has the rotated size, which matches the Display already sent.
prs.design:
Why. Each new picture is copied full-size (BGRA) before the video processor converts it: 0.1-0.2 ms per picture on a discrete GPU, 0.5-1.3 ms on an iGPU at 4K, plus memory-bandwidth contention; repeats rerun the video processor. A portrait or rotated display cannot be shared at all (capture unavailable, retried forever). An odd-sized desktop that needs no downscale (1365x767 under 1080p limits) is resampled by about 0.999, half-pixel-blending text across the screen. Downscaled sessions use OPTIMAL_SPEED processing.

1. Direct convert (R3-direct-convert), video/mod.rs submit: allocate the sample first, so MF_E_SAMPLEALLOCATOR_EMPTY returns Full before anything is acquired and the picture keeps accumulating in DXGI. On a new BGRA8 present: VideoProcessorBlt from the acquired surface into the sample through a small input-view cache keyed by texture pointer; Flush, then ReleaseFrame; hold the submitted sample as `last`. A repeat, keyframe or refinement on a still desktop copies CopySubresourceRegion from last's texture and subresource (converter.rs:191-201 shows texture arrays) into a fresh sample. Fall back to today's BGRA copy when CreateVideoProcessorInputView refuses the duplication surface (and, later, for FP16 frames). Drop `latest`, keeping the first-frame rule and the present stamps from capture-anchored-pacing.
2. Rotation (R3-rotated-display): accept DXGI_MODE_ROTATION_ROTATE90, 180 and 270, and treat UNSPECIFIED as identity. The output size comes from the rotated dimensions ((height, width) for 90 and 270) passed to scaled_size. Converter::new takes the rotation: check D3D11_VIDEO_PROCESSOR_FEATURE_CAPS_ROTATION through GetVideoProcessorCaps and call VideoProcessorSetStreamRotation(processor, 0, true, ROTATION_90/180/270), as airhand host/encoder/mf.rs:199-253 and Microsoft's DXGIDesktopDuplication sample do; the source rect stays the unrotated texture, the destination rect and VideoProcessorSetOutputTargetRect are the rotated output. On the first frame compare the texture's GetDesc with ModeDesc and fail with a clear error on a mismatch. Without the cap keep today's error. Input needs no change (desktop.rs:92-108 already maps the rotated orientation).
3. Odd edge (R3-crop-odd-edge): a neutral pure `crop_only(input, output)` in new crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/scale.rs (true when each input dimension is at most 1 above the output's; airhand host/encoder/mod.rs:149-151, mf.rs:221-235), unit-tested on every platform. When it holds, Converter::new sets the source rect to (0, 0, width, height) of the output (rotated dimensions under rotation), so the processor copies 1:1 and drops the last column or row. Input mapping is unchanged: the Display keeps its geometry and the missing edge pixel is off-video.
4. Downscale quality (R3-vp-quality-scaling): in Converter::new use D3D11_VIDEO_USAGE_OPTIMAL_QUALITY when the output is smaller than the input, OPTIMAL_SPEED for 1:1, through a per-vendor table (adapter VendorId) that stays empty until the device run shows a gain at under 1 ms of processor time; video_bench `--vp-usage quality|speed`. A shader area-filter downscale is the follow-up only if neither usage gives acceptable text.
5. Docs: Windows capture paragraph (direct conversion, rotated displays); CHANGELOG bullets (rotated displays can be shared; odd sizes stay sharp).

prs.name: win-present-waiter
prs.title: Windows host: make DXGI a push source, a capture thread that waits for the present when thread C arms it, converts at once and wakes thread C
prs.protocol_changes: None in process. Through the helper its notices reach the host only with helper-push.
prs.design:
Why. Thread C still polls DXGI: every 2 ms for 250 ms after input or a new picture, once a period otherwise. The first spontaneous change after stillness (a notification, a progress bar, a remote-initiated redraw) waits U(0, period): 8.3 ms mean at pace 60, 16.7 ms at 30. Up to about 500 capture calls a second each run two desktop verifications, a DPI scope and AcquireNextFrame. In process the present-to-capture wait is about 1 ms mean (2 ms polls) instead of a wake latency of 0.1-0.3 ms.

1. Encoder::build keeps creating the device and duplication on thread C, then spawns a capture thread (new platform/windows/video/capture_thread.rs) owning the IDXGIOutputDuplication, the context and the converter behind a SAFETY-commented Send wrapper where windows-rs does not mark them Send. In the helper worker its first call is SetThreadDesktop(GetThreadDesktop(thread C's id)), before any COM or D3D call; in process it inherits the desktop.
2. States. Unarmed: wait on an event while DXGI accumulates. Armed (thread C's tick is due and nothing was taken): loop on AcquireNextFrame(16 ms). On a present (LastPresentTime non-zero, or the first frame): AllocateSample (an empty allocator publishes 'no room' and stays armed); convert straight into the sample with the direct path from win-capture-convert; Flush, then ReleaseFrame; publish (sample, Presented { at: the present Instant, presents: summed AccumulatedFrames }), disarm, and call Waker::wake.
3. Thread C: submit takes the published sample and calls ProcessInput; a repeat or keyframe on a still desktop copies the held last sample; idle_until as MacVideo's: None when a picture is published or a keyframe is due, last_submit + LIVENESS_INTERVAL otherwise, FIRST_SUBMIT_WAIT before the first picture. VideoSource drain_poll and capture_poll both return None when the MF watcher runs (fully push); an encoder in the polling fallback (no IMFShutdown) keeps capture push and drain polled.
4. Errors (DXGI_ERROR_ACCESS_LOST and the like) are published and returned by the next submit.
5. Drop sets stop, signals the event and joins (at most 16 ms) before the Codec and the Runtime drop.
6. The present Instant is the stamp the anchored pacer consumes. video_bench gains a still run and a spontaneous-change run (the pattern changes once a second with no input) and prints capture_calls_per_s and polls_per_s.
7. Docs: Windows host paragraph (push capture), Diagnostics; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.title: Windows host: capture FP16 (HDR) desktops and tone-map them to SDR on the GPU using the display's SDR white level
prs.protocol_changes: None.

Why. With Windows HDR (or Auto Color Management) on, DXGI converts the FP16 desktop without the display's SDR white level, so the shared picture's brightness and contrast differ from the local view: washed-out mid-tones when the SDR brightness slider is above 80 nits.

Direct conversion stays BGRA8-only (FP16 frames take this path).

prs.name: win-still-refinement
prs.title: Windows host: sharpen a picture after it stops changing with a short burst of repeats that never spends the capture tick
prs.protocol_changes: None. Repeats are Video units with duplicate=true, which every v2 viewer already presents (protocol.rs:257-259; only its doc comment changes). HELPER_PROTOCOL, ALPN, FFI and viewers are unchanged; v10's `submitted: false` already means 'keep the tick armed'.
prs.design:
Why. Media Foundation encoders on NVIDIA budget per frame (measured nominal; remote-desktop.md:1568-1590), so after a scroll or window switch stops, a liveness repeat every 250 ms refines by one frame's budget: about 33 KB/s at Balanced 1080p against the session's 500 KB/s. Easy text that needs about 40 KB sharpens about 1.25 s after the stop, dense text needing about 480 KB takes about 14 s (estimates); a burst at the pace would take about 0.28 s and 1.2 s. (On the Mac the burst brings nothing, measured: scratchpad notes/r9_refine.txt; its dropped-picture re-send is in mac-vt-rate-control.)

Merged from R9-still-refinement-burst and the duplicate R3-static-refine:
1. Neutral policy `Repeats` in new crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/codec/refine.rs with an injected clock: fresh(at, pts), repeated(at), output(pts, duplicate, keyframe, len, qp: Option<u32>), repeat_now(now, last_submit), next_due(last_submit). One call per platform site.
2. A burst starts REFINE_AFTER = 200 ms (const-asserted below LIVENESS_INTERVAL) after the last fresh picture, and only when a fresh unit since the last burst was rate-limited: its size at least about 75% of the per-frame budget (bitrate / nominal fps under RateModel::Nominal). Typing echoes and caret blinks are small and already sharp, so they never start a burst (no latency cost, no wasted repeats).
3. Repeats come at the capture pace, at least one pace period apart (pace_fps stored in set_rate), with duplicate = true, and never spend the tick (Submit::Refined, spends_tick() false). A fresh present or an IDR request cancels the burst.
4. A burst stops at the first of: two consecutive non-keyframe repeats under REFINE_DONE_BYTES = 512 after REFINE_MIN = 3 repeats (guards the starved-first-repeats pattern); a repeat whose MFSampleExtension_VideoEncodeQP (when the MFT sets it) is at or below a floor or has not dropped for two repeats; REFINE_MAX_TIME (start 1 s, at most 15 repeats, final value from the device bench). Only outputs newer than the last fresh pts count. After a burst today's 250 ms liveness rule applies unchanged.
5. Source: the held last-submitted NV12 sample (win-capture-convert), copied with CopySubresourceRegion into a fresh sample; no video processor rerun.
6. Enable per vendor by adapter VendorId / MFT friendly name; the list is filled only from the device run (NVIDIA first). An MFT measured to budget by timestamp stays off; thread C's rate-model latch does not reach the encoder.
7. Windows wiring (video/mod.rs, capture_thread.rs): lines 513-518 become one repeat_now call; record fresh or repeated after ProcessInput; call output where collect builds Encoded; Statistics.refined. video_bench: --still <ms>, a GDI-text pattern with a freeze flag, per-unit lines after the freeze, --dump-source.
8. If the device shows a typing-echo cost above 1 ms mean despite the trigger, the soft tick (a fresh picture may follow a refinement repeat after P/4 instead of 3P/4) is a follow-up after win-phase-locked-decimation, which owns the next pacer and helper change.
9. Docs: the duplicate meaning in protocol.rs, Diagnostics (presented_fps and present_interval change after a stop), constants table; a benchmark record including the Mac burst-off rationale; CHANGELOG bullet with measured figures.

prs.title: Windows helper: skip the worker's cold H.265 probe on later sessions by caching its answer in the host process per adapter and driver
prs.protocol_changes: Helper pipe: StartCaps gains `adapter: Option<AdapterKey { vendor_id, device_id, subsys_id, revision, driver_version: u64 }>` (serde default, omitted when None, deny_unknown_fields kept). Bump HELPER_PROTOCOL by one above master's value at merge (11 if nothing else bumped since 10) and rename both pipes to .v<n> (helper/mod.rs PIPE and helper/background.rs PIPE, kept in step by names_protocol). Desktop wire and ALPN unchanged.
prs.design:
Why. Every privileged session (the recommended 'Turn on remote control' path, ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/host.rs:521-525) runs in a fresh worker. When the viewer decodes H.265 the worker probes H.265 cold before Accepted (Request::H265, oop/server.rs:162-169): 320-350 ms in a fresh process, 951 ms the first time after a build (remote-desktop.md:1415-1420), and Accepted waits for it (acceptor.rs:332-354). The host process (the app or the background host) outlives sessions.

1. The worker's Start answer reports the capture adapter's key in StartCaps: VendorId, DeviceId, SubSysId and Revision from DXGI_ADAPTER_DESC plus the UMD driver version (IDXGIAdapter::CheckInterfaceSupport); LUIDs change across reboots, so they are not the key (merged from the duplicate R9-M3-helper-probe-cache). Cheap DXGI queries in platform/windows/video/probe.rs.
2. RemoteBackend keeps a process-wide cache {AdapterKey -> h265: bool}, bounded at 8 entries. describe(true) answers from it without sending Request::H265; a miss probes as today and fills the cache.
3. H265_FAILED, which thread C sets when the worker reports EncoderFailed{H265}, already stops describe(true) for the rest of the process; additionally clear that key's entry so a later process state cannot reuse it. A wrong cached answer costs what a failed H.265 build costs today: one capture_failed and a reconnect to H.264.
4. Both ends validate the new field (bounded integers).
5. Docs: helper protocol history in remote-desktop.md; the user-guide pair (English and Chinese) and CHANGELOG say the Windows desktop service must be updated (Update installs it).
(av1-windows-host extends the cache to (key, codec) and probes AV1 concurrently.)

prs.name: native-cursor
prs.title: Desktop viewers: show host pointer shapes as native OS cursors and switch them without waiting for a Flutter frame
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire, Rust or FFI. A new runner method channel `pb_mapper/desktop_pointer` (cursor_create, cursor_set, cursor_delete) on all three desktop runners, with its Dart client and test fake.
prs.design:
Why. A controlling desktop viewer over a custom or upArrow shape hides the OS pointer and has Flutter paint the bitmap at the last hover position, so that pointer trails the hand by Flutter's event-to-present pipeline, about 1.5-3 refreshes (25-50 ms at 60 Hz) and feels floaty next to the hardware cursor shown over named shapes. It happens often: Mac hosts name only 7 standard cursors (platform/macos/cursor.rs:134-142), so open or closed hand, context menu, drag-copy and the window-corner resizes are custom; Windows hosts name 14 shared handles (platform/windows/cursor.rs:20-35), so every cursor an app loads itself (browser grab, Office, Adobe, CAD) is custom. A Mac viewer also lacks system cursors for busy, move and diagonal resizes from Windows hosts. A shape change today waits for a MouseRegion rebuild and the post-frame MouseTracker pass. airhand scales host cursors to the picture (client/src/lib/session.ts:802-821).

1. A new channel `pb_mapper/desktop_pointer` in new runner files, so the desktop_video runners stay untouched (viewer-scroll and relative-pointer add their methods to the same files): `cursor_create {id, rgba (straight alpha), width, height, hot_x, hot_y}` (physical pixels after Dart's scaling), `cursor_set {id}`, `cursor_delete {id}`. Do not use the engine's own Windows cursor methods.
2. Windows (ui/windows/runner/desktop_pointer.{h,cpp}, constructed in flutter_window.cpp like DesktopIme): CreateIconIndirect from a 32-bpp top-down DIB section (BGRA) and a 1-bpp mask derived from alpha; DestroyIcon on delete; ::SetCursor on the platform thread. The engine's WM_SETCURSOR returns TRUE for HTCLIENT without setting a cursor (flutter_window.cc:725-731), so the runner's cursor stays until Dart activates a system cursor, which MouseTracker does on enter and exit.
3. macOS (ui/darwin/DesktopPointer.swift under #if os(macOS), registered in ui/macos/Runner/MainFlutterWindow.swift and added to the macOS Runner target in project.pbxproj): NSCursor(image:hotSpot:) from an NSImage holding an NSBitmapImageRep at pixel size, size and hotspot in points (pixels / backingScaleFactor); set(). If the FlutterView responds to `didUpdateMouseCursor:`, call it with the cursor so the engine's cursorUpdate: restores ours; otherwise re-set it from a cursorUpdate local monitor.
4. Linux (ui/linux/runner/desktop_pointer.{h,cc}, registered in my_application.cc): gdk_cursor_new_from_surface (a cairo image surface with the device scale) and gdk_window_set_cursor on the FlView's window, the one the engine uses (fl_view.cc:158-166).
5. Dart: new ui/lib/src/ffi/desktop_pointer.dart client (and test fake). In remote_cursor_layer.dart add `RemoteShapeCursor extends MouseCursor`; RemotePointerRegion passes one constant instance while mouse && controlling. Its session listens to RemotePointer, DesktopCursor.shape and the viewport scale and calls the platform directly on activate and every change, with no rebuild. Kinds the viewer OS has go through SystemChannels.mouseCursor activateSystemCursor (mapping per viewer platform; on macOS wait, progress, help, move and both diagonal resizes take the bitmap path). Kinds it lacks, plus upArrow and custom, take the bitmap path: scale by picture scale x devicePixelRatio, clamped to 0.35-2 and at most 128 logical px; cache per (content, scale within 2%), at most 16 like _shapeCache; cursor_delete on eviction, at session end and on dispose. When not atLocalPointer, as today.
6. Painting stays for viewers that do not control, for touch, and as the fallback when a channel call throws.
7. Docs: the viewer pointer section; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.title: Windows host: inject pointer moves with absolute SendInput instead of SetCursorPos
prs.protocol_changes: None (Input::Move unchanged; helper requests and responses unchanged).

WinInput::pointer (platform/windows/input.rs:53-58) sends one INPUT_MOUSE with MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE | MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE | MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK, plus MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE_NOCOALESCE while any button is held (track it in WinInput from button()); coordinates normalized to 0..65535 from SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN read in the thread's per-monitor-aware DPI context and cached until a display change; dwExtraInfo = enigo.get_marker_value(), as send_physical already does.

5. Docs: Windows input paragraph; CHANGELOG bullet.

(b) Pointers the viewer does not draw locally (the host user's, another controller's, an app-moved one) are reported and read at a fixed 62.5 Hz even in a 120 fps session. Host (Rust):
1. Engine (worker.rs) gains `shape_due: Option<Instant>`: set to now + 2 ms after a Move is injected for a slot that negotiated cursor_shapes (worker/control.rs:390-405), only while self.cursor_shapes; after that look allow one more at +8 ms for slow apps; at most one pending, a new move restarts the 2 ms look.

Watchers get an extra position report only together with a new shape. deadline() (worker.rs:968-993) includes shape_due. Through the helper, cursor_shape() still crosses the pipe only when shape_serial moved; the Windows hot polling after input refreshes that serial.
3. Cursor cadence (R10-pointer-cadence): while capturing, cursor_due = now + CURSOR_INTERVAL.min(self.pacer.period()).max(8 ms).
Viewer (Dart):
4. RemoteCursorLayer gets a derived ValueNotifier<RemoteCursorPaint?> recomputed from viewport, cursorChanges and pointer; it notifies only when the paint result changes (null to null never does), and the painter repaints from it.

prs.name: viewer-pixel-snap
prs.title: Desktop viewers: keep a 1:1 picture on the device-pixel grid and show a near-1 fit at exactly 1:1
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. Original-size mode sets exactly one remote pixel per physical pixel (remote_viewport.dart:280-286), but autoScrollTo (227-252) and the fitted centring (fittedRect, 73-83) produce fractional offsets, and the scene is placed by a Transform with that translation (remote_surface.dart:260-273). The texture is sampled bilinearly, so at a half-pixel offset a 1-pixel text stroke becomes two half-intensity pixels, and in original-size mode text alternates between sharp and blurred on every pointer move; the same happens at a fitted 1:1 whose centring falls between pixels (Windows at 125% or 150%). airhand shows a picture up to 4% smaller than its area at 1:1, aligned to device pixels (client/src/lib/fit.ts:1-6, 14, 55-61; docs/architecture.md:213). This is display-side only, not J (encoding the window's size), which stays rejected.

1. RemoteViewport learns the stage's global origin in physical pixels: _ViewportSync or RemoteSurface's LayoutBuilder reads localToGlobal(Offset.zero) after layout and passes it with devicePixelRatio.
2. Snap: whenever the effective scale is 1:1 (original mode, or abs(scene.width x scale x dpr - remotePixels.width) < 0.5), _set snaps the offset so (origin + offset) x dpr is an integer: offset = round((origin + offset) x dpr) / dpr - origin. This covers autoScrollTo, relayout and pinch end, never an active pinch.
3. Near-1 fit: in fit mode, when the fit scale in device pixels s = min(roomPx.w / remote.w, roomPx.h / remote.h) is in [1, 1.04), use exactly 1:1, centred and snapped.
4. toNormalized and toLocal already use the same offset and scale, so input mapping stays exact. Native presenters (mac-viewer-layer, linux-video-plane) follow Flutter's transform, so they inherit the snap.
5. CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: rate-model-latch
prs.title: Latch the Timestamp rate model from per-tick integrated bits within about 2 s
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. The latch needs two consecutive 3 s windows at pace <= 0.75 x nominal (qos.rs:667-688), so a per-second encoder (AMD or Intel MFTs if they budget per second, SDK backends) overspends nominal/pace times for 6 s or more after every pace drop, and a mid-window bpf cut can latch a per-frame encoder falsely, which receipt-driven rate control would trigger often.

1. qos.rs: tick() diffs ProducedSnapshot every 250 ms into 8 fixed buckets (a sliding 2 s span). Each bucket holds frames, unique frames, non-IDR bits, integrated expected bits (bpf at that tick x the non-IDR frames of that tick) and a paced-low flag.
2. Latch Timestamp when the 2 s span has at least 6 unique frames, every bucket was paced at or below 0.75 x nominal, and non-IDR bits > max(1.3, 0.6 x nominal / mean pace) x the integrated expected bits. The second term stops a per-frame encoder at its content floor from latching (NVIDIA measured up to 1.79 at pace 5 with nominal 120, remote-desktop.md:1586-1592); a per-second encoder overshoots by about nominal/pace and still latches.
3. close_window keeps only the bpf step; the latch stays one-way and keeps its trace.
4. slow_link.rs: Sizes::PerSecond, bytes = bitrate x (now - previous capture) / 8 with the gap capped at 1 s, modelling a per-second encoder including its burst after idle.
5. Docs: the rate-model paragraph and constants.

prs.design:
Why. (1) Every congestion signal today is a round trip, so a standing queue on the viewer's upload (cloud backup, photo sync, a video call, cellular uplink) collapses a perfectly good forward link: bits per frame fall 15% every 3 s, admission caps near 25 fps by the frame window and the byte window spirals to its 32 KiB floor, ending around 5 fps for as long as the 60 s RTT minimum stays clean; a 200-600 ms Wi-Fi uplink stall delays probes and receipts alike and halves fps. airhand acks every frame with its arrival time (crates/airhand-link/src/flow.rs:6-17, 269-316). (2) A recovering viewer that asked for an IDR still receives every P-frame made before it, which it discards: on a 1 Mbit/s link 35 such frames over 8 requests, about 250 ms of link time against a median wait of 399 ms (requested_idr_on_a_slow_link at 1515eda).

A. Arrival time (R5-arrival-time-receipts, merged duplicate R8-receipt-arrival-time).
1. Protocol constants in protocol.rs; the viewer lists arrival_time (viewer/config.rs) and fills at_us only when Accepted listed it.
2. Viewer: Reader::run takes `let at = Instant::now()` right after read_header_with returns (viewer/session.rs:278-288) and passes it to handle; outbound.receipt(seq, at) keeps (max seq, its at) in the slot and outbound.probe(nonce, at) likewise (viewer/outbound.rs:191-197, 315-321); Outbound::next writes at_us. No allocation. No Dart or runner change.
3. Host write, only for a session whose viewer listed the capability: write_message_with (wire.rs) gets a split mode, write_all(records = header length, header, payload length) then write_all(payload) and one flush, so the header is its own small TLS record and the viewer stamps the unit's first bytes, not the end of a 16 KiB record. No copy is added; other sessions keep the single vectored write.
4. New platform-neutral crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/oneway.rs: `WindowMin`, a monotone deque over RTT_WINDOW (60 s) with at most one sample per 250 ms bucket and capacity reserved once (at most 256 entries; no per-receipt allocation). `OneWay` holds one forward WindowMin shared by receipts and probes (same clock offset), one reverse WindowMin and a 3-slot ring of recent reverse queues. sample(at_us, sent_host, recv_host) returns forward = (at - sent) - min_f and reverse = (recv - at) - min_r, both saturating at 0, in i64 microseconds against SessionShared.epoch. Validity (never authority): ignore a sample whose at_us goes backwards or whose one-way delay exceeds IO_TIMEOUT above the minimum; only a malformed message is a protocol violation. reset() wherever qos.reset_baseline runs (Path, session.rs:412) and in Qos::resume. No clock-jump rule (Instants are monotonic).
5. credit.rs: on_receipt(seq, now, at_us) samples OneWay for the newest covered unit; Receipt gains forward_queue and reverse_queue: Option<Duration>; when present, ack_samples store the forward queue and ack_queue returns its median with no base subtraction. window() uses t = base + WINDOW_MARGIN + min(min of the last 3 reverse queues, 1 s) (the conservative rule of the R8 duplicate: one delayed receipt never widens it); the frame and byte maximums, fits() and the JPEG window are kept.
6. qos.rs: on_probe_echo(nonce, now, at_us, ack_queue): with at_us the probe's forward queue feeds history/delay_ms and raw; RTT still feeds rtt, base_rtt, last_rtt, short_path and FAST_START; tainted handling unchanged, the witness is the forward ack_queue. qos/receipt_rate.rs (the shadow estimator) takes the forward queue and viewer-clock spacing; receipt-rate-control consumes these values instead of adding its own timing.
7. Diagnostics: StatsRecord forward_queue_ms and reverse_queue_ms (only to a viewer that listed the capability), carried to the quality panel through the existing viewer status op: FFI JSON (ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/viewer.rs), Dart DesktopViewerStatus (desktop_models.dart), a panel row, the test fake; host trace fields too.
B. Keyframe seq (R8-keyframe-seq-skip).
8. The outbound keyframe slot (viewer/outbound.rs:206-207, 366-367) stores (reason, seq). `after_seq` carries the Reader's last read seq at the moment of the request, and is set only when the request comes with the sink discarding P-frames until the next IDR (its wait_key; the sink passes this with the request). Never for User. With viewer-fps-cap's age episodes, which keep decoding queued units, a Backlog request does not set it; overflow, Gap, DecoderError and Stall do. The seq is needed because receipts outrank Keyframe in the viewer's writer.
9. Host: B-recv's Keyframe handler (session.rs:368-371) still requests the IDR; it sets a session flag skip_to_keyframe only when the credit ledger has booked no keyframe with a seq above after_seq (the ledger gains last_keyframe_seq). B-send (session/sender.rs:407-440) pops and drops this session's non-keyframe units before booking them, exactly as it drops a stale generation's, so seq stays contiguous; they count in dropped_frames. The flag clears when a keyframe is admitted or after 2 s. Other viewers in a room are unaffected; it never touches the host's own resyncs (unlike B's withdrawn hand-off supersede).
C. Tests: protocol round trips; an old host never receives at_us or after_seq and an old viewer never gets the Stats fields (viewer/tests.rs); oneway minimum tracking, bound, reset, a large constant offset of either sign, backwards samples ignored; credit: a reverse delay widens t, the forward queue drives the clamp; qos: a reverse-only delay never cuts, a forward delay cuts as today; skip only when no keyframe was booked above after_seq, the flag clears on admission or after 2 s.
D. Docs: send credit, QoS, viewer recovery and the capability list in docs/remote-desktop.md; benchmark record; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: receipt-rate-control
prs.title: Receipt-driven rate control (D stage 1): cut bits per frame within a round trip, keep the frame rate, and cut fps only from the delivery rate at the preset floor
prs.protocol_changes: None (wire, helper pipe and FFI unchanged; VideoRate already travels with each capture call).
prs.design:
Why. Receipts feed only send credit; frame rate and bits per frame follow the 1/s or 4/s probe, fps by RustDesk delay steps and bpf every 3 s in 5-20% steps (qos.rs:600-661, 664-731). Congestion therefore costs frame rate first: the recorded 1 Mbit/s case ends at pace 10 while bpf hardly moves (docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-desktop-pipeline/slow_link.txt). Stage 0 already ships the shadow estimator (qos/receipt_rate.rs: standing_ms, busy_bps, would_cut) and Receipt {delay, bytes, behind_idr} from credit.rs. airhand does all rate control on per-frame acks (crates/airhand-link/src/flow.rs:555-616, cut min(0.85 x busy, 0.9 x estimate), episodes and rebase, raise 15%/s or 4%/s near capacity).

Build stage 1 of the D design (scratchpad research D-fast-rate-control), adapted:
1. receipt_rate.rs acts: on_sample returns a Verdict {None | Hold | Cut(target_bps) | Rebased}: raw = delay - base minus the frame allowance (min(frame interval, bytes x 8 / busy)); rebase tracked as a minimum (receipt-local, the probe base untouched); standing = min of the last 3 queues, before = min of the 3 before; skip samples behind an IDR; busy = median per-pair rate over the last 8 pairs where the link stayed busy (None below 3); congested = standing > QUEUE_HIGH (40 ms) || (blocked && standing > QUEUE_LOW (10 ms)), with `blocked` counted only while the window is clamped. Congested: inside a hold nothing; draining (standing + 5 ms < before, or < 0.8 x the episode's last) -> Hold; two cuts that left it within 1.1x -> Rebased; no busy rate -> None (no blind cut, the probe controller remains). Stage 0's stall and burst rule stays as it is.
2. Cut and hold (R8 (g)): hold until both max(rtt + standing, 100 ms) has passed and used <= 1.1 x target, for at most 1 s. Cut to min(0.85 x busy, 0.9 x used), or 0.85 x used when stalls recur. Remember capacity = busy.
3. qos.rs cut_to(target): p = pace, floor = preset floor x pixel scale; if target/p >= floor: bpf = min(bpf, target/p), adaptation LoweringBitrate; else bpf = floor and rate_fps = Some((target/floor).max(min_fps).min(p)), adaptation LoweringFps. pace() adds .min(rate_fps) before the startup, unresponsive and JPEG clamps. One owner for `adaptation`; Quality keeps its order: bpf to bpf_start/2, then fps from the delivery rate, then bpf to the floor.
4. Raise on the 250 ms tick when samples are fresh, no hold or episode, standing < QUEUE_LOW, rebase not growing and used >= 0.5 x expected: credit += per_s x dt (dt <= 500 ms; 0.04 near capacity (>= 0.9x), else 0.15) plus 100 kbit/s per second; apply at >= 5%; clear capacity above 1.2x. With rate_fps set, lift the fps cap first. Recovery accelerator, required (R8 (b)): when an episode has ended and standing has stayed under 10 ms for >= 500 ms, raise at 50%/s toward 0.9 x the expected rate held when the episode began, once per episode, skipping the 4%/s band; if that climb is cut below 0.9 x that rate, fall back to 15%/s and 4%/s.
5. Ownership and baseline (R8 (a)): control_fps yields to receipts only while an episode is active or within 2 s of a receipt cut or rebase (no 'standing < 40 ms' term); in the >= CUT_DELAY branch an owned arm holds fps below SEVERE_DELAY (600 ms); without ownership, or at >= 600 ms, today's arms run unchanged. On Rebased record rebase_offset = own_min - probe_base capped at CUT_DELAY (150 ms); control_fps computes delay against probe_base + rebase_offset; clear the offset when the 60 s probe base itself rises past it and on Path, resume, set_preset and reset_baseline, so both controllers share one baseline and queue creep is bounded by 150 ms plus the probe steps.
6. One-way inputs (R8 (d)): when arrival_time is negotiated (viewer-feedback), standing and busy come from the forward queue and viewer-clock spacing; otherwise from RTT receipts with stage 0's allowance.
7. Balanced H.264/H.265 starts at its ceiling whatever the first probe's RTT: remove the FAST_START_RTT gate at qos.rs:503-505 (receipts now cut within a round trip) (R8 (e)).
8. close_window: the rate-model latch is unchanged (rate-model-latch made it per tick, so mid-window cuts never latch Timestamp); step_bpf is skipped when receipts produced samples since the window started; JPEG and windows without receipts keep today's step.
9. Resets: set_preset -> fast.reset() and rate_fps = None; resume -> restart (samples, episode, hold); reset_baseline -> reset including rebase, capacity and rebase_offset.
10. session.rs and sender.rs: Session gains `blocked: AtomicBool`; admissible() reads qos.clamp_rate(now) and passes it to credit.window (credit.window gains `clamp: Option<u64>`: during an episode bytes = (DELIVERY_FACTOR x rate x t / 8).clamp(BYTE_WINDOW_CLAMP_MIN, normal), applied immediately); when fits is false and no IDR is in flight, under the same credit lock, store blocked = true; handle Received swaps it into qos.on_receipt; lock order unchanged (no credit and qos nesting). The feedback trace gains bpf, rate_fps, standing_ms, busy_bps, rebase_ms, cuts.
11. Mac hosts shed bandwidth with the fps part only with the Timestamp start (mac-vt-rate-control); VideoToolbox's response to a cut is measured and handled there (R8 (f)).
12. Decision record: DECISIONS D5 and CONTRACT-perf R13 (docs/remote-desktop-overhaul/plan/DECISIONS.md) say the probe owns fps and bitrate with receipts only clamping the byte window; record this deviation and the user's directive explicitly, as DECISIONS.md:1-5 requires.
13. Docs: QoS, send credit, constants; benchmark record indexed in docs/README.md; CHANGELOG bullet saying the rate target changes within a round trip, with measured figures only.

prs.name: reconnect-start-rate
prs.title: Start a reconnecting viewer's session at the rate the previous session ended at
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. Reconnects happen most on slow links, yet each new session starts at the preset's bpf_start: Balanced's first 1080p IDR is about 267 kbit at bpf_start against about 67 kbit at the floor (Quality about 800 against 200), and the startup pace of 30 x bpf_start is 2 Mbit/s on a 1 Mbit/s link, a queue bounded only by the 2x window (about 0.5 s of data at a 36 ms base). Estimate: the first picture after a reconnect on 1 Mbit/s arrives about 0.2-0.6 s sooner.

1. The host Room (host.rs) keeps one record: the bpf of the last session that ended by transport loss (End::Closed or HOST_READ_TIMEOUT), relative to 1080p, its preset, and when it ended.
2. A session accepted within 2 min with the same preset starts with bpf = min(the preset's start, the remembered bpf, rescaled to its picture). Qos::new takes an optional start (session.rs:198 passes it). Balanced's fps fast start is unchanged. A record older than 2 min, or from another preset, is ignored; the record only ever lowers the start.
3. A different viewer on a fast link within 2 min starts lower and climbs at the receipt controller's rate (receipt-rate-control's accelerator).
4. Docs: QoS startup paragraph; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: encoder-throughput-cap
prs.title: Cap the pace at the encoder's measured throughput when units queue four deep, so dwell falls back to one or two service times
prs.protocol_changes: None. The pace Stats already report reflects the cap. No helper field (see design).
prs.design:
Why. When a Media Foundation encoder is slower than the pace and serial at its bottleneck while still accepting input, four units queue and each waits behind three: an 11 ms encoder at pace 120 has about 44 ms dwell, uneven. Capping the pace at what it delivers gives 11-16 ms with even spacing. NVIDIA is unaffected (3.1 ms at 4K); AMD and Intel at 4K or 1440p 120 are unmeasured, so how often this triggers is shown by its trace. Mac hosts are covered by their submit thread's two-in-flight gate and the H.265 standard-RC switch.

Simplified from the proposal: no Backend::encoder_full and no helper `full` field. After win-mf-output-events, Submit::Full means only MAX_IN_FLIGHT (= ENCODER_DEPTH, which thread C already sees as pending_video() >= ENCODER_DEPTH) or a rare empty sample allocator; the serial-before-NeedInput case is Submit::Waiting, which keeps the tick armed and builds no queue.
1. worker/window.rs counts full ticks per second (ticks where pending_video() >= ENCODER_DEPTH), apart from transport skips, with units produced and dwell p50.
2. Rule: full ticks >= max(2, pace/10) in a second set cap = max(the preset's min_fps, floor(0.95 x units)); after 3 s without a full tick the cap rises by max(1, cap/20); it clears at the QoS pace.
3. Apply it in capture_step's min pace (worker/capture.rs) and publish it as an AtomicU32 in each slot's SessionShared (shared.rs) that the session hands to its Qos (session.rs), whose pace() takes min with it (qos.rs, like viewer_cap at qos.rs:590-597).
4. Pipelined guard: keep the dwell p50 of the second before capping; if 2 s after capping dwell p50 is not below 0.6x of it, lift the cap and do not cap again for 30 s (latency, not throughput, filled the queue).
5. Trace `desktop_encoder_cap` {cap, full_ticks, units, dwell_before, dwell_after}.
6. Docs: the pacing paragraph and Diagnostics; CHANGELOG bullet only with device evidence of a vendor that triggers it.
