prs.name: viewer-fps-cap
prs.title: Viewer: remember the decoder's capacity in the fps cap, raise in steps scaled to the ceiling, and drain an age backlog instead of freezing until the IDR
prs.protocol_changes: None (no protocol, FFI or runner change; fixed rings, no allocation per unit).
prs.design:
Why. (a) A consumer slower than the host (Linux software decode, Windows software MF in VMs, 4K120 on weak iGPUs) overshoots about every 5-6 s; most overshoots end in an age drop, a frozen picture until an IDR arrives and an IDR bandwidth spike; slow_presenter's mean pace is 12.4 for a 14.9 fps consumer. (b) At a 120 ceiling a transient backlog that halves the cap to 60 takes about 14 s to clear (CAP_STEP 5 per second after a 3 s hold). (c) On an age backlog the sink drops the queue at push (sink.rs:399-402) and take (599-601) as soon as the head is 250 ms old with 3 queued, sets wait_key and discards every later P-frame, so a consumer whose thread stalled 300 ms then returned shows nothing until the IDR (250 ms + RTT + encode + IDR transfer, over a second on 1 Mbit/s). airhand drains moderate backlogs and resets only beyond 8 queued in the decoder or 120 frames (client/src/lib/video.ts:34-35, 108-112, 171); its cap probes 15%/s far from capacity and 4%/s near it.

All in viewer/sink.rs and viewer/fps_cap.rs:
1. Signals per 250 ms tick: pulls (units take() handed out); backlogged tick (queue non-empty at both ends, no restart or drop between); measured capacity = pulls in backlogged ticks over their time across the last 8 ticks, valid once >= 4 backlogged ticks (1 s); head wait (age of the queue head); consumer lag: record presented_at - handed_at (sink.rs:704-741) in a 128-slot ring, excess = median over the last 1 s minus minimum over the last 10 s (near 0 on Darwin and Windows; grows by a decode time per hidden unit on a saturated Linux pipeline).
2. Lowering: today's triggers (a drop or backlog episode, or more than 2 queued on two ticks) plus excess consumer lag over max(2/cap s, 40 ms) on two ticks. capacity = the measured capacity when valid, else presented_fps; cap = floor(capacity x 0.9 direct or 0.8 relayed), at least CAP_MIN; the halving bound applies only when capacity came from presented_fps. Remember capacity and when.
3. Raising: with no known capacity, or up to hold = floor(0.95 x capacity): 3 s hold then one change a second, step = max(CAP_STEP x max(1, round(ceiling / 30)), ceil(0.25 x cap)) (R10's ceiling scaling: 20 at 120, 10 at 60, 5 at 30, merged with R5's 25% step). Above hold a raise is a probe: step max(1, ceil(0.1 x capacity)), allowed only after probe_backoff since the last failed probe (3 s doubling to 60 s, reset by a successful probe).
4. Probe watch (3 s after a probe): one tick with (>= 2 queued and head wait > max(2/cap s, 40 ms)) or excess consumer lag above the same reverts at once to the pre-probe cap (exempt from CAP_CHANGE_MIN) and doubles probe_backoff; a probe that survives forgets capacity and resets the backoff.
5. Forget capacity on a new generation, a picture-size change or a preset change.
6. Age backlog drains (R5-drain-age-backlog): on age, at push or take, when no age episode is open: open one, request the IDR through Recovery as today (KeyframeReason::Backlog; limiter and backoff unchanged, so the request time is unchanged), count it in backlog_drops (its meaning becomes 'backlog episodes'), tell the fps cap once, and do NOT clear the queue or set wait_key; keep enqueueing. The episode closes when an IDR is pushed (which already supersedes the queue with discontinuity, sink.rs:377-394) or the head's age falls below BACKLOG_AGE/2. Overflow (32 units, 8 MiB) still drops to the next IDR exactly as today. Recovery is unchanged (the awaited-IDR episode ends only when the IDR or a later frame is presented); the stall watchdog is unchanged.
7. Unchanged: CAP_MIN, the factors, the ceiling and its removal (sending max_fps), freeze() and the 500 ms IDR_GRACE judging.
8. Docs: 'Viewer: newest decodable frame, fps cap and recovery' and the sink module doc; CHANGELOG bullet with measured figures.

prs.name: mac-viewer-layer
prs.title: macOS viewer: present each decoded 420v picture on a native Core Animation layer from the decoder thread, skipping VideoToolbox's BGRA pass and Flutter's frame
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire, capabilities, helper or FFI; receipts still go through pb_mapper_desktop_video_presented_v1. App-internal pb_mapper/desktop_video channel only: a 'presenter' argument on create, a 'grey' method, a platform view type 'pb_mapper/desktop_video_view', and timings.present in stats.
prs.design:
Why. Today the Mac viewer decodes to BGRA (VideoToolbox's conversion pass: 33 MB written per 4K frame) and hands a CVPixelBuffer to a Flutter texture, so each picture waits for Flutter's next frame on the merged platform/UI thread, then raster and composite. Measured here (paced 60 fps): decode 0.7-1.3 ms less per frame at 1080p and 3-4 ms less at 4K with 420v; the first picture after stillness 3-6 ms sooner at 4K (scratchpad notes R6-macos-viewer-measurements.txt, r6rev_vt*.swift). Estimated from the Flutter source: about one refresh less from decode to glass (12-16 ms at 60 Hz, 6-8 at 120, 5-7 at 144), no jitter from a busy UI thread, lower power, and video that keeps moving during a live window resize. airhand presents on decode off the UI thread.

Scope: macOS only (#if os(macOS)); iOS and a macOS escape hatch (--dart-define=presenter=texture) keep the texture path; the presenter is chosen per viewer at create.
Swift (ui/darwin/DesktopVideo.swift):
1. create takes presenter: 'layer'|'texture' and still replies with an Int id; in layer mode the id comes from the plugin's own counter with no FlutterTexture registration; the texture limit and instance check are unchanged.
2. In layer mode VideoDecoder.attributes asks for kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarVideoRange with IOSurface properties and Metal compatibility (kept for mac-viewer-enhance).
3. Colour: in layer mode, after describe(), always rebuild the format description with TransferFunction = kCMFormatDescriptionTransferFunction_sRGB (10.13+; the app targets 10.15), primaries 709 and the stream's matrix (709 when absent), regardless of withBt709's early return and the VUI. At configure check the first decoded buffer carries the sRGB transfer attachment; if VideoToolbox did not carry it, set it per picture with CVBufferSetAttachment(.shouldPropagate) before the commit.
4. LayerPresenter, created at create (commits can precede the view): a container CALayer and a content CALayer (isOpaque, contentsGravity .resize, linear filters, autoresizing width and height). present(picture) on the feed thread: CATransaction.begin(); setDisableActions(true); content.contents = CVPixelBufferGetIOSurface(buffer); CATransaction.commit(). Keep the last three CVPixelBuffers referenced and set `shown`. Then copyPixelBuffer's receipt logic: under the lock the revision check, presented += 1, timings.present from decode end to commit end; after the commit, outside the lock, library.presented. publish() calls the presenter instead of hopping to main. No layer property is touched on that thread outside an explicit transaction, no NSView there.
5. DesktopVideoView: NSView, layer-hosting (layer = container before wantsLayer = true); default hitTest; acceptsFirstMouse true; acceptsFirstResponder false (keys stay with FlutterView); no mouse, scroll or magnify overrides (NSResponder forwards to FlutterView); layerContentsRedrawPolicy .never; layerUsesCoreImageFilters true. 6. 7. grey {textureId, on} on the main thread: content.filters = [CIColorMatrix with GreyStill's coefficients (viewer_overlays.dart:395-400)] or nil.
8. While attached and not paused, on macOS 14+, an NSView.displayLink asks preferredFrameRateRange up to the screen's maximum; its callback only counts, while stats timings are on, commits beyond the first in each refresh as `dropped`; before 14 a CVDisplayLink for that counting only. Keep the frame-rate request only if the ProMotion device check shows it is needed.

prs.name: viewer-refresh
prs.title: Desktop viewers: follow the refresh rate of the display the window is on, exactly (59.94, 119.88 on Windows), with the existing FpsCap message
prs.protocol_changes: No wire or capability change: reuses ViewerMessage::FpsCap (protocol.rs:188-191), which every peer accepts, and limits.max_fps at connect. FFI: one new op `{"op":"display_refresh","hz":<f64>}` of the existing pb_mapper_desktop_viewer_call_json export, changed on every side at once (Rust export, Dart DesktopApi interface, implementation, FakeDesktopApi). Windows runner: a `refresh_hz` method on the app's own pb_mapper/desktop_video channel.
prs.design:
Why. (a) The viewer asks for its display's refresh only at connect (and on macOS the fastest screen), so a Smooth session whose window moves from a 120 Hz to a 60 Hz screen keeps encoding, sending and decoding 120 fps of which half are superseded, at half the bits per frame; moving back does not resume 120 without a reconnect. (b) Windows viewers on 1000/1001 modes (59.94, 119.88 Hz: TVs, HDMI timings, some panels) ask 59 or 119 because Flutter reports whole hertz, so a 60/120 Hz host loses about one present a second while content moves: a hitch every second.

Rust (viewer/fps_cap.rs, sink.rs, mod.rs):
1. FpsCap gains `display_fps: Option<u32>` and `display_changed: bool`, set through set_display(fps). ceiling = if fps_override { max_fps } else { min(ceiling_fps(preset), max_fps, display_fps) } (a user-chosen rate ignores the display: the frames are fresher).
2. `release` = display_fps.filter(|d| !fps_override && *d < max_fps).unwrap_or(max_fps): the value meaning 'no backlog cap'. Every place that sends max_fps today sends release instead, including the raise-to-ceiling branch, so a backlog recovery never clears the display limit.
3. On display_changed the next tick sends the new effective value at once, bypassing CAP_CHANGE_MIN, the high-tick gate and the 3 s raise hold: min(backlog cap, display) when lowering, release when no backlog cap; while frozen (paused) it applies at the first tick after resume. Backlog lowering (viewer-fps-cap's capacity logic) keeps working beneath the display ceiling.
4. sink.rs set_display_fps; Viewer::set_display_refresh(hz: f64) rounds and clamps to MIN_VIEWER_FPS..=MAX_FPS as VideoLimits::choose does (Android ignores it, as choose does); session.rs:583-585 already forwards what tick returns. video.rs: a unit test pins 59.94 -> 60 and 119.88 -> 120.
FFI and Dart:
5. ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/viewer.rs: DisplayRefresh { hz: f64 } op, with its Dart interface (desktop_api.dart), implementation and fake.
6. Windows runner (desktop_video.cpp): WindowRefreshHz(HWND): MonitorFromWindow on the Flutter view's HWND, GetMonitorInfoW for szDevice, QueryDisplayConfig(QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS) with DISPLAYCONFIG_DEVICE_INFO_GET_SOURCE_NAME matching viewGdiDeviceName, returning that path's targetInfo.refreshRate exactly; else dmDisplayFrequency. Exposed as `refresh_hz`.
7. New ui/lib/src/ffi/display_refresh.dart: the window's display refresh; on Windows the runner's refresh_hz (bounded at 200 ms, falling back to the current value); elsewhere PlatformDispatcher's view display refreshRate.
8. desktop_store.dart: on macOS, Windows and Linux connect with that refresh as refresh_hz (desktop_store.dart:341, displayMaxHz); a PlatformDispatcher.onMetricsChanged listener (plus window focus and move on Windows) sends display_refresh whenever the value differs from the last sent, and once after connect. Android unchanged.
(The Mac runner's refreshHz stat already reports the window's screen, from viewer-decoder-stats.)

prs.name: linux-gpu-convert
prs.title: Linux viewer: keep decoded pictures on the GPU, converted in Flutter's GL context through an FlTextureGL (module ABI 2, dma-buf where available)
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire or the FFI. The runner-module C ABI goes from 1 to 2 (bump PB_VIDEO_MODULE_ABI to one above master's value at merge); both are built together and the ABI check (desktop_video.cc:109) rejects a stale module. File and symbol names stay.
prs.design:
Why. Today every hardware-decoded picture is downloaded to system memory (NV12: 3.1 MB at 1080p, 12.4 MB at 4K), converted to RGBA on the CPU by up to 4 videoconvert threads (desktop_video_gst.cc:88, 575-579), and re-specified into Flutter's texture as RGBA (8.3 or 33 MB). Estimated saving: 4-12 ms of CPU per 1080p picture and 15-40 ms per 4K picture across threads, which matters for laptop battery and thermals and makes 1440p or 4K at 60+ possible on iGPU laptops. Merged duplicate: R10-linux-gpu-convert (same goal; it also notes Flutter's Linux embedder takes at most 60 frames a second, so at 120 fps half of today's CPU conversions are discarded).

Design (the corrected one: no GstGL on the default path, the module stays GL-free and hands over the decoder's native picture; the runner converts in whatever GL context presents it, so no context bootstrap, no cross-context sync and no new runtime package):
1. Measurement commit first: module stats gain `timings.decode`; the harness prints CPU ms per decoded picture per thread from getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD).
2. Module ABI 2 (desktop_video_module.h:79-111): pipeline appsrc -> parse -> decoder -> appsink with no videoconvert; appsink caps video/x-raw,format={NV12,I420}; add video/x-raw(memory:DMABuf),format=DMA_DRM,drm-format=<NV12 with the modifiers the presenter imports> only when the presenter reports dma-buf import and GStreamer >= 1.24; a decoder that offers none of these gets videoconvert to NV12. Candidates (166-223) accept decoders whose source pad offers system memory or DMABuf. create takes the presenter's capabilities (dma-buf import yes/no, modifier list). New describe(picture, PbVideoPlanes*) gives visible width/height and format, colour matrix and range from the caps (DefaultColorimetry keeps its BT.709 default), and per plane either {data, stride} or {dmabuf fd, offset, stride, drm fourcc, modifier}, using GstVideoMeta offsets so 1088-row surfaces crop. `pixels` is replaced by snapshot(picture, max_width, rgba out), which for system memory uses a GstVideoConverter scaling straight to <= 320 px. The module links gstreamer-allocators-1.0 (in libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev).
3. Runner GL helper, new ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_gl.cc (epoxy, which libgtk-3-dev brings): plane textures R8/RG8, or LUMINANCE/LUMINANCE_ALPHA on ES2 without EXT_texture_rg, updated with glTexSubImage2D (GL_UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH where available, else padded rows with scaled texture coordinates); or per-plane EGLImages (eglCreateImageKHR(EGL_LINUX_DMA_BUF_EXT, DRM_FORMAT_R8/GR88, modifier), cached per pooled buffer, glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES). One shader pass (BT.709 or BT.601, limited or full range, from describe) into an RGBA8 GL_TEXTURE_2D through an FBO, saving and restoring every GL binding it touches as fl_compositor_opengl.cc:222-245, 348-358 do. An EGL fence after the pass; a picture returns to GStreamer only once its fence signalled (checked without waiting at the next call); hold at most 2 pictures. Capabilities read on the GTK thread at create without a context: eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT on GDK's native display (the EGLDisplay fl_opengl_manager.cc:47-61 obtains; initialize if needed, never eglTerminate), EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import(_modifiers), eglQueryDmaBufModifiersEXT for NV12; GL_OES_EGL_image confirmed at the first conversion, else the runner tells the module, which falls back to system memory at the next keyframe and asks for one once.
4. PbVideoTexture becomes an FlTextureGL subclass (desktop_video.cc:228-303): populate acquires the newest picture (the receipt), converts it and returns GL_TEXTURE_2D/GL_RGBA8 (suits Skia and Impeller); before the first picture a 1x1 black texture. For dma-buf pictures the helper refreshes an RGBA readback of <= 320 px at most once a second for snapshot. FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software keeps today's path.
5. Optional NVIDIA stage (NVDEC GLMemory through CUDA-GL interop) only if device numbers show NVDEC's download plus YUV upload still costs more than about 2 ms per 4K picture.
6. Build and CI: runner/CMakeLists.txt links epoxy; the module adds gstreamer-allocators-1.0; syntax-check.yml linux-app adds libegl1, libegl-mesa0 and libgles2 for the harness. No new runtime package in the user guide (no gstreamer1.0-gl).
7. Harness (ui/linux/test/desktop_video_test.cc:104-200): a surfaceless EGL ES2 context (llvmpipe) stands in for the raster thread and calls the helper; checks the converted texture is GL_TEXTURE_2D RGBA8 of the picture's size, glReadPixels of the converted test pattern matches videoconvert's RGBA of the same picture at PSNR >= 40 dB (BT.709 limited), the snapshot is non-uniform, and the software (libav I420) path decodes with no videoconvert.
8. Docs: 'macOS, iOS and Linux decoders' (remote-desktop.md:2204-2266); CHANGELOG bullet with device figures.

prs.name: linux-presenting-gpu
prs.title: Linux viewer: decode on the GPU that presents the window (hybrid laptops, multi-GPU desktops)
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire or FFI. Module ABI bump (one above master's value at merge): probe and create take the presenting render node.
prs.design:
Why. Candidates are ordered hardware first, then registry rank (desktop_video_gst.cc:187-223, sorted at 219-221), with no regard for which GPU renders the window. Candidates order hardware decoders by 'on the presenting device', then rank: va per-device factories (va<renderDNNN>h264dec) name their node, the default vah264dec is the first render node; nvcodec maps cuda-device-id -> PCI bus id -> /dev/dri/by-path/pci-<bus>-render; vaapih264dec uses LIBVA's default node.

prs.name: linux-video-plane
prs.title: Linux viewer: present video on a GTK GL plane under a transparent FlView, off Flutter's fixed 60 Hz clock
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire, FFI or module ABI. The runner channel `pb_mapper/desktop_video`: the create reply gains `plane`, a new `place` method, `grey` implemented for the plane, and stats gain planeIntervalP50Ms/P95Ms and refreshIntervalMs. The Dart DesktopVideoTexture interface and its fakes change with it.
prs.design:
Why. Every Linux viewer presents at most 60 fps through Flutter's fixed timer (proven from the pinned 3.44.9 sources); each picture waits for that timer, unsynchronised with the display (mean about 8 ms), then raster, populate and compose, then GTK's frame clock. With a plane: 120 Hz+ monitors on Smooth get up to 120 fps on Wayland (GNOME, KDE, wlroots) and Mutter X11; every user loses one unsynchronised wait plus 1-4 ms of Flutter work (estimate 8-13 ms off the mean at 60 Hz); on X11 a video picture no longer triggers a full-window glReadPixels.

1. Runner (my_application.cc:59-78): the FlView becomes the overlay child of a GtkOverlay whose main child is a new PbVideoPlane, a GtkGLArea in ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_plane.cc (has-alpha FALSE, auto-render). The plane starts hidden and the FlView background stays opaque black. Only while a plane-backed viewer has placed a visible rect: show the plane and fl_view_set_background_color(#00000000) (takes effect on the next draw, fl_view.cc:862-867); revert on visible=false or dispose. Outside a session nothing changes.

prs.name: mac-viewer-enhance
prs.title: macOS viewer: optional GPU enhancement of an enlarged picture (clamped Catmull-Rom plus luma-only sharpening) through a CAMetalLayer, and the shared 'sharpen enlarged picture' preference
prs.protocol_changes: None: app-internal channel method `enhance {textureId, level}`.
prs.design:
Why. A 1920x1080 or 2560x1440 host full-screen on a 3024x1964 to 3456x2234 Retina panel or a 4K/5K external is enlarged 1.2-1.8x bilinearly today, so text is soft. airhand offers luma sharpening with peaks off/low/medium/high = 0/-0.06/-0.1/-0.14 (client/src/lib/enhance.ts:22) and plans the presenter by on-screen size. Off by default, it costs nothing; on, one or two GPU passes at display size (airhand quotes about 0.5 ms on an RTX 4080 laptop; unmeasured on this M6).

Builds on mac-viewer-layer, macOS only:
1. A second presenter mode, active only while enhancement is on and the on-screen pixel size is at least the picture's on both axes (below that the plain YUV layer, as airhand's renderPlan). The on-screen size is the layer bounds converted to the window's root layer times backingScaleFactor, recomputed in layout() and when the mutator transform changes.
2. A CAMetalLayer beside the plain content layer; a switch toggles their isHidden in one main-thread transaction, so the picture never blanks. CAMetalLayer: .bgra8Unorm, sRGB colourspace, framebufferOnly, maximumDrawableCount 3, drawableSize = on-screen pixels.
3. A presenter thread with a newest-wins slot: the feed thread puts the decoded 420v picture there and returns at once. The presenter thread wraps both planes through CVMetalTextureCache (R8, RG8; zero copy); pass 1 converts with the BT.709 limited-range matrix and no transfer conversion (same sRGB look as the plain layer) and upscales with 9-tap Catmull-Rom clamped to the 4 nearest texels into a private intermediate texture (skipped at exactly 1:1); pass 2 applies CAS-style luma-only sharpening with airhand's peaks into the drawable; commit with present. The receipt and timings.present are taken at the scheduled present. It keeps the last picture and redraws when the geometry or level changes. Shaders compile at run time from a source string (MTLDevice.makeLibrary(source:)), so no .metal resource or project-file change.
4. Snapshot keeps using the decoded buffer.
5. Dart: a per-device preference 'Sharpen enlarged picture' (off, low, medium, high; default off) in viewer_prefs.dart and the viewer's Display menu (viewer_menus.dart), sent through `enhance {textureId, level}`, offered only when the texture has a native presenter. linux-plane-scaling reuses the same preference for its plane. Strings in both locales; icons from AppIcons.
6. Docs and CHANGELOG.

prs.name: viewer-scroll
prs.title: Scrolling: one wheel notch is one host notch on every viewer, high-resolution (1/120-notch) scrolling by capability, and trackpad momentum carried to the host
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: host capability `wheel_hires` (from a new BackendCaps.hires_wheel, listed in BackendCaps::values()); new `Input::Scroll { horizontal: i32, vertical: i32, continuous: bool }` in 1/120-notch units (continuous serde default, skipped when false), |v| <= 12000 in Input::validate, sent only to a host that listed wheel_hires (Viewer::input returns NotOffered otherwise). Helper pipe: Input::Scroll crosses it and StartCaps gains hires_wheel: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names (.v<n>). No FFI export change (the existing input op carries Input JSON). Runner channel pb_mapper/desktop_pointer gains `wheel_lines` (Windows).
prs.design:
Why. (a) remote_surface.dart turns every PointerScrollEvent into notches at kWheelPxPerNotch = 30 logical px (:19, :229-238), but each embedder reports one wheel notch as a different distance: Windows lines x 100/3 physical px (flutter_window.cc:468-478, 798-808; flutter_windows_view.cc:660-661), i.e. 100/DPR logical at 3 lines; macOS 40 logical per line (FlutterViewController.mm:735-757); Linux 53 (fl_scrolling_manager.cc:108). One Windows notch at 100% sends 3,3,4,3 notches (9-12 lines on a Windows host); macOS and Linux send 1,1,2 and 2,2,1 patterns. (b) A 30 px trackpad move becomes a whole notch: 3 lines (about 100 px) on a Windows host, 1 line on a Mac host, so remote content jumps in steps and scrolls about 3x too fast on Windows hosts. (c) Flutter drops OS scroll momentum on every desktop platform (macOS skips momentum-phase events, FlutterViewController.mm:614-625; Windows suppresses DirectManipulation inertia, direct_manipulation.cc:73, 152; GTK/libinput produce none), and pb-mapper reads raw PanZoom in a Listener (remote_surface.dart:213-226), so a fling stops dead on the remote computer. airhand forwards OS momentum as wheel events (client/src/lib/input.ts:518-530).

1. Notch fidelity (R4-wheel-notch-fidelity; every host, old ones included, no protocol): for a mouse-kind PointerScrollEvent, notches = delta / pxPerNotch with pxPerNotch per viewer platform: Windows 100 x lines/3 / devicePixelRatio, macOS 40, Linux 53; the carry stays. `lines` comes from `wheel_lines` on the Windows runner's pb_mapper/desktop_pointer channel (SPI_GETWHEELSCROLLLINES; 3 if the call fails). Trackpad PanZoom and trackpad-kind scroll keep their own distance per notch.
2. Units (R4-hires-scroll): 120 = one notch = 100 logical px of continuous travel. Protocol as above; Outbound::submit sums a single-Scroll batch onto a tail Scroll of the same generation and continuity (beside outbound.rs:249-261), so a trackpad flood never fills the 512-event queue.
3. Dart _wheelBy, when capabilities contain wheel_hires: PointerPanZoomUpdate and trackpad-kind PointerScrollEvent -> units = px x 1.2, continuous; a mouse PointerScrollEvent -> units = notches x 120 (notches per step 1), continuous = false; a carry per axis. Without the capability send today's notches at the corrected per-platform notch size.
4. Host: Injector::scroll(h, v, continuous) has a default that accumulates whole notches into wheel(); native.rs maps Scroll; thread C re-aims the pointer before Scroll as before Wheel (worker/control.rs:458-470). Windows: one SendInput carrying MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL mouseData = -vertical and/or MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL mouseData = horizontal (only the nonzero ones). macOS: continuous posts CGScrollEventUnit::Pixel with px = units / 1.2 (points) with a carry and kCGScrollWheelEventIsContinuous = 1; discrete stays CGScrollEventUnit::Line at units/120 lines with a carry (one line per notch as today). The synthetic backend lists the capability so desktop_ui_host logs Scroll.
5. Momentum (R4-trackpad-momentum), Dart in RemoteSurface: track PanZoomUpdate pan deltas with a VelocityTracker (trackpad kind, event timestamps); on PointerPanZoomEnd above kMinFlingVelocity run a Ticker-driven decay with the viewer platform's physics (macOS's 0.998/ms deceleration as BouncingScrollSimulation's friction; a ClampingScrollSimulation-like curve on Windows and Linux); each tick sends the integrated delta through _wheelBy (continuous Scroll units with wheel_hires, else notches with the carry). Cancel on PointerScrollInertiaCancelEvent, a new PanZoomStart, a pointer down, a discrete wheel event, focus or control loss, or a generation change. Outbound summing bounds the queue.
6. Helper: bump as above, one record of the bump in the remote-desktop.md protocol history.
7. Docs and CHANGELOG: the Platforms table (remote-desktop.md:1132), the Constants Input row, the 'a notch per 30 px' text (:237-238); the user-guide pair if it mentions scrolling or the helper update.
Legacy guard: if a classic Win32 listbox or a Java Swing list fails to scroll under continuous input on a device, add a viewer setting to turn smooth scroll off.

prs.name: standby-session
prs.title: A warm standby session on the other path: survive a dead direct path in about 1.5 s and upgrade a relayed session to direct
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: capability `standby` both ways; optional `Accepted.ticket` (32 bytes from ring's SystemRandom, base64url) and `Authenticate.standby_for`, each sent only to a peer that listed the capability (serde default, omitted when unset). No relay wire or DIRECT_VERSION change. SDK: a #[doc(hidden)] `Client::connect_tcp_direct` (no PathPolicy variant, no ConnectOptions field). No FFI or Dart change (logic inside Viewer); no helper-pipe change (HostStatus keeps its shape).
prs.design:
Why. A direct-specific failure (a NAT rebinding or firewall that kills the punched path while the relay is alive) costs an estimated 8-9 s outage today, with the room emptying and display modes restored in between; a relayed session that fell back transiently stays on the relay for its life (the deployed TCP relay measured a 194 ms median ping, docs/remote-desktop.md:2533). Two ordinary sessions, no splice, no new ALPN.

1. When standbys open. A relay standby opens only for an internet-direct primary (punched or port-mapped QUIC), never for LAN QUIC or LAN TCP. A direct-only standby opens only after a NegotiationTimeout, NegotiationFailed or Unreachable fallback; it obeys the shared cooldown (direct-cooldown) and the NetworkHints generation, is never tried after NotOffered, reuses one Consumer and Network per Viewer across attempts, and records its own outcome (it must not log session_path_selected path=relay or count as a fallback).
2. Protocol as above.
3. Host acceptor: check the token first in constant time, then the ticket in constant time over SHA-256 digests. A standby takes a standby permit (one per active slot), starts paused, causes no room keyframe, and does not appear in HostStatus or in peer cursors.
4. Promotion is a Resume on the standby. Under the room lock the room moves display-mode ownership, the admission lease and the ticket to the promoted slot, then ends the primary with End::Closed. Held input is released at the primary's end, failing closed. The resume IDR is forced; reset_baseline runs only if the route differs. Restore runs when the pair ends.
5. Viewer, new viewer/standby.rs: promote at once on a transport error on the primary, or when the primary has had no bytes for max(1.5 s, 4 x base RTT) while the standby received at least one message in that interval; promote a committed direct standby at once (default order, no RTT gate). Attach the standby to the VideoSink with a discontinuity so it waits for the IDR (sink.rs:377-386), then swap the metrics connection slot; document that an earlier subscribe_metrics stream ends at a switch.
6. Telemetry, trace only: desktop_viewer_promoted{cause, outage_ms}, desktop_viewer_standby{route, outcome}.
7. Established direct sessions keep belonging to the endpoints: coordinator loss, revocation or relay rejection never close them (CLAUDE.md invariants unchanged).
8. Docs: the user-guide pair, the remote-desktop.md lifecycle and constants, a relay operator note (one extra relay stream per internet-direct viewer); CHANGELOG bullet. Keep each capability list within MAX_CAPABILITIES.

prs.name: helper-push
prs.title: Helper protocol: the worker pushes encoded units, fresh-picture notices (with present age) and pointer updates; thread C stops long-polling the pipe
prs.protocol_changes: Helper pipe: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names (.v<n>). Between replies the worker may send tagged records, all deny_unknown_fields: {kind:'unit', generation, video: VideoFormat, pending} followed by its bytes record; {kind:'fresh', presented_ago_us, presented_count}; {kind:'pointer', cursor, shape_serial}. Replies are tagged {kind:'reply', ...Response}; the Video reply gains presented_ago_us: Option<u32> and presented_count: Option<u8> for the submitted picture (serde default, omitted when None). Request gains Stream{on}; Request::Video loses wait_ms (DRAIN_WAIT_MAX_MS goes). Both ends validate: a unit is at most ipc::MAX_FRAME, its generation matches the host's expected context, pending <= 64, the pointer lies inside the display, ages over 1 s are ignored, unknown kinds are rejected. prs.design:
Why. Each iteration serves queued requests first; then, while Stream{on}: drain finished units and send Unit plus its bytes record (one vectored write_record from helper-pipe-transfer); when the armed source has published a fresh picture, send Fresh{presented_ago_us, presented_count} once per armed present (the age computed just before writing); every 16 ms read the pointer and send Pointer only when it or the shape serial changed. prs.name: win-phase-locked-decimation
prs.title: Windows host: at a pace that is an integer fraction of the refresh, capture every k-th present as it lands instead of a stale picture at a grid tick

prs.design:
Why. capture-anchored-pacing anchors only when the pace equals the present rate. When the pace is an integer fraction of the refresh (Quality's 30 on 60 Hz, Balanced 60 on a 120 Hz host, 72 on 144 Hz, 40 on 120 Hz) the grid takes whatever picture is newest at its tick, a picture up to a source period old. Model (scratchpad notes r9/align.py, continuous content, 2 ms polls): mean present-to-capture wait 3.2-8.8 ms -> 0.55-0.9 ms; mean event latency 60 Hz/30: 15.8-17.1 -> 9.1 ms; 120 Hz/60: 8.0-8.3 -> 4.8 ms; 144/72: 6.7 -> 4.0 ms; 120/40: 11.8 -> 8.9 ms; frame rate unchanged within 0.5%. On the Mac, mac-capture-cadence already makes ScreenCaptureKit deliver every k-th vsync at an exact multiple, and the anchored pacer takes each on arrival, so this PR is Windows-only.

1. Lock (pacer.rs): the source presents continuously (the last 4 dated captures each took k new presents, from Presented.presents); the source period is known (DXGI_OUTDUPL_DESC.ModeDesc refresh); k = round(refresh / pace) >= 2 and |refresh/k - pace| < pace/64.
2. While locked the next capture targets the predicted k-th present after the last one taken, at last_stamp + k x Pd: the window opens Pd/4 before it; a waiting picture stamped earlier than predicted - Pd/4 is not taken while the prediction is still due; it is taken anyway at predicted + 1 ms if nothing newer came; the floor stays last + 3P/4, so the rate is bounded by the display.
3. Thread C passes the target as a 'not before' stamp through a provided Backend method (forwarded in the five impls), an internal VideoSource argument (DXGI's capture thread returns Unchanged for an older picture), and through the helper as Request::Video/Stream.not_before_in_us.
4. Non-integer ratios (45 on 60 Hz, 60 on 144 Hz) and non-continuous content keep today's behaviour byte for byte.

ClientInner (sdk/client.rs:36) gets `direct_memory: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<DirectMemory>>`: at most 64 entries, evicting expired ones first, keyed by (relay endpoint identity, namespace, service key); each entry holds the Cooldown, the TCP Cooldown and the network generation of its last back-off.

prs.name: host-direct-bbr
prs.title: BBR on the desktop host's direct QUIC (the video sender), once receipt-driven control owns the rate
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire (congestion control is sender-local). No public RegisterOptions field: a #[doc(hidden)] Client method; no Node, CLI or helper-pipe change.
prs.design:
Why. On WAN direct paths with random loss of about 0.1% or more and RTTs of 50 ms or more (cross-border links, cellular hotspots, long-haul paths), Cubic's loss response caps the video sender's throughput and slows IDRs and scroll bursts. BBR is not limited by random loss. Nothing changes on LAN or clean paths. On policed uplinks only receipt control protects the path, hence the ship order.

1. A #[doc(hidden)] Client method, e.g. `register_with_sender_congestion(request, options, SenderCongestion::Bbr)`, threading a crate-private choice through DirectPolicy (direct_policy.rs:17-24) to the provider Network::new (direct/provider.rs:301), identity.server and transport(), which sets congestion_controller_factory(Arc::new(quinn::congestion::BbrConfig::default())). pb-mapper-desktop's host.rs:383 calls it, compiled in, so the Windows background host needs no helper-pipe field.
2. The consumer side, generic tunnels and the relay QUIC carrier stay on Cubic.
3. DirectLink (non_exhaustive) gains a controller label so device traces tell the two apart.
4. pb-mapper-testkit: new lossy_udp(loss, delay, rate_bps): a per-direction ordered queue after airhand crates/airhand-link/src/lib.rs:85-150, with a seeded PRNG and raised socket buffers; test-only (its per-packet copies never reach a data path).
5. New example crates/pb-mapper-desktop/examples/direct_cc_bench.rs: two quinn endpoints with pb-mapper's direct TransportConfig through the forwarder; 60 fps P-frames of 8.3 KB and a 150 KB IDR every 2 s under the credit window, with echoed receipts.
6. Ship only if the bench gates below pass; otherwise keep Cubic and record why.
7. Docs: transport section (sender congestion control); CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: relay-tcp-tuning
prs.title: Linux relay: disable TCP slow start after idle (Docker sysctl, opt-in install step, startup notice) and opt-in BBR on relay sockets
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire. Relay server option `--tcp-congestion <name>` (env PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION, read at startup only), off by default, added to RelayServerOptions following its existing pattern without breaking public struct literals.
prs.design:
Why. (a) Linux restarts a TCP connection's congestion window from IW10 after an idle period (net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle = 1), so on relayed sessions the first scroll, window switch or IDR after a still period slow-starts: an estimated 100-400 ms more latency on that first burst over 50-150 ms legs. (b) With Cubic the relay->viewer leg's throughput ceiling is about 1.2 x MSS / (RTT x sqrt(p)): roughly 0.9 Mbit/s at 1% loss and 150 ms, below every preset's rate, so pace and bpf collapse on lossy cross-border and cellular legs; kernel BBR (mature BBRv1/v3 with a decaying bandwidth filter) is not limited by random loss.

1. docker/docker-compose.yml: `sysctls: net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle: 0` with a comment that it needs Linux 4.15+ and is namespaced to the container; a commented line for the congestion option.
2. scripts/install-server-github.sh and -gitee.sh: an opt-in prompt that writes /etc/sysctl.d/90-pb-mapper.conf.
3. pb-mapper-server on Linux, at startup: read /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_slow_start_after_idle; when 1, log one info event relay_tcp_idle_restart naming the fix (read-only).
4. `--tcp-congestion <name>`: on each accepted relay socket (connection.rs:117-121) set TCP_CONGESTION best effort (socket2's set_tcp_congestion); on EPERM or ENOENT log once with the fix (modprobe tcp_bbr plus net.ipv4.tcp_allowed_congestion_control, or CAP_NET_ADMIN in Docker). Only the relay's sending direction changes, which carries the relay->viewer video leg. Opt-in keeps zero cost by default; the fairness trade-off is the operator's choice.
5. Docs: an operator note in the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) and DOCKER_README.md; CHANGELOG without figures.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (option parsing; the sysctl reader as a pure function over file content); `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. prs.name: disposable-frames
prs.title: Disposable (temporal-layer) frames: shed frames without an IDR on slow decoders and stop a room following its slowest viewer
prs.protocol_changes: None: both ends read NAL headers (nal_ref_idc / HEVC temporal ids). No helper change: the bit is derived from bytes the session already holds.
prs.design:
Why. A slow-decoder viewer (Linux software decode at 4K, older laptops) that falls behind today flushes its sink and forces an IDR on each backlog drop (slow_presenter recorded 3 drops and 3 requested IDRs in 10 s even before viewer-fps-cap), and in a multi-viewer room a drop at the hand-off forces an IDR for everyone while the shared stream follows the slowest viewer's pace (worker/capture.rs:224-227). Disposable (non-reference) frames can be shed without breaking the reference chain. Conditional on encoder compliance and efficiency, which Phase 0 measures.

Phase 0 (gate), on this Mac, ignored release tests in platform/macos/tests.rs reusing L's grain pattern and PSNR: (a) the default low-latency stream's share of non-reference units; (b) kVTCompressionPropertyKey_BaseLayerFrameRateFraction 0.5 with BaseLayerBitRateFraction 0.6: the disposable share and bits against a single layer at equal PSNR; (c) decode tolerance: drop the disposable units and decode the rest with VTDecompressionSession (decode feature for tests only), zero decode errors. Windows: a video_bench probe of CODECAPI_AVEncVideoTemporalLayerCount per vendor (device). Go on only for encoders with a disposable share >= 1/3 at a bitrate cost <= 5% at equal PSNR, or already present by default.
Phase 1: codec/annexb.rs marks `disposable` beside the IRAP check, carried on HostUnit and UnitMeta; Outgoing::push, when full, drops a disposable unit first without setting needs_keyframe; the viewer sink's backlog handling (episodes from viewer-fps-cap) drops queued disposable units before falling back to drop_to_idr; enable that drop on Media Foundation and GStreamer viewers only after a device check of each decoder.
Phase 2: rooms send base-layer units only to a viewer whose own pace is at most half the room's (session/sender.rs), and capture's minimum over viewers (worker/capture.rs:224-227) counts only viewers that keep up.
Zero cost: turn layers on by default only if Phase 0 shows they are free; otherwise only in rooms of two or more (encoder settings in platform/macos/encoder.rs on the submit thread and platform/windows/video/codec.rs).
Docs: room and sink sections; CHANGELOG with measured figures.

CI rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, nat-traversal.yml.

Phase 1, 3 release runs each before and after: slow_presenter with a synthetic encoder marking every other unit disposable (backlog_drops, keyframes_requested, presented fps); a two-viewer room with one viewer shaped to 1 Mbit/s (host keyframes and the fast viewer's received fps): `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 slow_link`; host_send_bench allocations unchanged.
